```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")

# -- Simulation control -------------------------------------------------------
nsims_alt   <- 200L
nsims_null  <- 200L
sim_seed    <- 8316951L
n_workers   <- max(1L, floor(0.95 * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))

# -- FS diagnostic capture (priority D) ---------------------------------------
# run_simulation_analysis() can attach the full forestsearch() and GRF
# result objects to the first N replicates via keep = / keep_first_n =.
# Set diag_keep_first_n > 0 to enable diagnostic capture; set to 0L to
# disable (and save memory).  Default 20L gives Section 7's per-sim detail
# print and the cross-sim subgroup frequency summary in @sec-results.
diag_keep_first_n <- 20L
diag_keep         <- c("fs_full", "candidate_table")

# -- Subgroup-distribution plot thresholds (Section 8.2) ----------------------
# plot_sg_distribution() displays only subgroup labels that appear in at
# least min_pct of the detecting sims.  Under H1 (many finds) a larger
# threshold keeps the bar chart readable; under H0 (rare finds, heavy
# fragmentation across labels) a smaller threshold keeps any bars at all
# above the line.  Adjust to taste.  Values are in percent (0-100).
sgdist_min_pct_alt  <- 0   # H1: identified & complement bars
sgdist_min_pct_null <- 0   # H0: identified & complement bars

# Cap on the number of bars shown in the subgroup-distribution charts.
# If more labels clear the min_pct threshold, the top sgdist_top_k are
# shown and the rest are pooled into a single "Other (k labels)" bar.
# Prevents unreadable charts under H0 when finds are fragmented across
# many singleton labels.
sgdist_top_k         <- 15L

# Whether to render the pooled "Other (k labels)" bar alongside the top
# sgdist_top_k.  Set FALSE to drop the pooled bar entirely, which keeps
# the axis tightly focused on the top labels.  Useful under H0 when the
# "Other" bar is so large that it compresses the top labels visually.
# The subtitle continues to report the suppressed count for honesty.
# Per-scenario so you can show the pooled bar under H1 (where it is
# typically small and informative) and hide it under H0 (where it may
# dominate).
sgdist_show_other_alt  <- FALSE
sgdist_show_other_null <- FALSE

# -- Effect-distribution violin y-axis limits (Section 8.2.3) -----------------
# plot_effect_distribution() can produce extreme OR values that dominate the
# display.  ylim clips the viewport via coord_cartesian (data are NOT dropped;
# violins, boxplots, and mean/SD annotations use the full dataset).
# Set NULL to let ggplot2 determine limits automatically.
ordist_ylim <- c(0, 6)

# -- Production projection targets --------------------------------------------
prod_alt               <- 5000L
prod_null              <- 25000L


# -- Dataset preparation: ACTG175 ---------------------------------------------
#
# ARMS (matching Leon et al. 2024, Section 4.2):
#   speff2trial::ACTG175 arm coding:
#     0 = zidovudine (ZDV) alone
#     1 = ZDV + didanosine (ZDV+ddI)   <- experimental
#     2 = ZDV + zalcitabine (ZDV+ddC)
#     3 = didanosine (ddI) alone        <- control
#
# The paper compared arm 1 (ZDV+ddI, combination) vs arm 3 (ddI,
# monotherapy) and searched for a BENEFIT subgroup Q by switching
# treatment roles.
#
# True subgroup anchor (used for DGM construction and ground-truth
# classification ONLY; NOT exposed to the analysis methods):
#   z1 (age):     age > 34        -- median split
#   z2 (preanti): preanti <= 745  -- q3 split
#
# Analysis candidate covariates are provided as described in the
# "Realistic analysis setting" block below.
actg_arms        <- c(1L, 3L)
actg_treat_arm   <- 1L
actg_age_cut     <- 34
actg_preanti_cut <- 744.5

# -- Benefit search via treatment switching ------------------------------------
# This vignette implements a BENEFIT search for the experimental treatment
# (ZDV+ddI) using two combined conventions, so the package's harm-search
# machinery points in the right direction (full table in the Appendix):
#
#   1. Treatment is switched (ddI = 1, ZDV+ddI = 0) — so a benefit subgroup
#      of the original experimental appears as a "harm" subgroup of the
#      switched-treatment.
#
#   2. The binary outcome is encoded on the IMPROVEMENT scale: y_binary = 1
#      when the patient improved (cd420 > cd40).
#
# Under these conventions, OR(Q) > c1 in the analysis means: the switched
# treatment (ddI) increases the odds of improvement in Q — equivalently
# ZDV+ddI decreases the odds of improvement in Q — i.e. ZDV+ddI harms
# in Q.  This is the benefit subgroup of ZDV+ddI.  Thresholds:
#   c1 = fs_or_threshold    (screening)
#   c2 = fs_or_consistency  (consistency)
# After identification, ORs are inverted to the original scale via
# subgroup_notation = "benefit".

# -- DGM construction ---------------------------------------------------------
# The DGM uses the discretised z1-z12 factor formulation because
# generate_glm_dgm() requires factor covariates.  The TRUE benefit
# subgroup is defined by {z1 = 1 AND z2 = 1}, i.e. age > 34 AND
# preanti <= 744.5.  This provides the ground truth for the
# sensitivity / PPV computations in run_simulation_analysis().
dgm_factor_vars   <- paste0("z", 1:12)
dgm_subgroup_vars <- c("z1", "z2")
dgm_subgroup_cuts <- list(z1 = 1L, z2 = 1L)
dgm_n_super       <- 5000L

# -- Treatment-effect scaling (k_treat) ---------------------------------------
# k_treat scales the fitted treatment main effect on the linear-predictor
# (log-odds) scale inside generate_glm_dgm():
#
#   eta_1 = eta_0 + k_treat * (eta_1_fitted - eta_0_fitted)
#
#   k_treat = 1 (default) preserves the fitted ACTG175 treatment effect.
#   k_treat > 1 amplifies the marginal ITT effect.
#   k_treat < 1 attenuates it.
#
# Two scenario-specific knobs so the H0 and H1 simulations can carry
# different baseline marginal effects independently:
#
#   dgm_k_treat_alt  -- applied to the calibrated alt DGM (used by both
#                       the initial alt build and the calibration grid).
#                       Calibration searches k_inter at this k_treat to
#                       hit cal_target_or, so changing this changes the
#                       k_inter that maps to OR(Q) = 2.0.
#
#   dgm_k_treat_null -- applied to the null (homogeneous-effect) DGM.
#                       Note: the null model represents a HOMOGENEOUS
#                       treatment effect (not a zero effect); k_treat
#                       scales the magnitude of that homogeneous effect.
#                       Useful for testing FPR under a stronger common
#                       benefit baseline.
#
# Both default to 1 so the existing operating-characteristic results are
# unchanged.  Set to a non-unit value to explore sensitivity.
dgm_k_treat_alt   <- 1.0
dgm_k_treat_null  <- 1.0

# -- Realistic analysis setting -----------------------------------------------
# The simulation mimics a real data analysis in which the analyst does
# NOT know which variables define Q nor the cuts that identify it.
# Continuous covariates are therefore supplied to forestsearch() and
# grf.subg.harm.glm() in their RAW form; the search methods discover
# cuts themselves (forestsearch: median / GRF-derived / forced cuts;
# grf.subg.harm.glm: policy-tree splits).
#
# NOTE: the true subgroup Q still involves age (continuous, cut at 34)
# and preanti (continuous, cut at 744.5).  Forestsearch will attempt
# cuts at medians and GRF-selected thresholds, which will generally
# DIFFER from the true cuts.  This is the realistic setting and is
# precisely what we want to evaluate: the method's ability to recover
# an effect subgroup when the cutpoints are unknown.
analysis_continuous_vars <- c(
  "age",      # continuous; TRUE cut (34) unknown to analyst
  "preanti",  # continuous; TRUE cut (744.5) unknown to analyst
  "wtkg",     # continuous
  "karnof",   # Karnofsky score (integer 70-100, treated as continuous)
  "cd40",     # baseline CD4 (continuous)
  "cd80"      # baseline CD8 (continuous)
)

# Truly binary indicators from ACTG175 (passed as factors to the
# analysis; no cut to discover).
analysis_binary_vars <- c(
  "hemo",     # hemophilia (0/1)
  "homo",     # homosexual activity (0/1)
  "drugs",    # IV drug use history (0/1)
  "race",     # race (0/1, white vs non-white as coded)
  "gender",   # gender (0/1)
  "symptom"   # symptomatic (0/1)
)

# -- Calibration ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Target OR(Q) = 2.0 on the switched scale (ddI = 1): in Q, ddI doubles
# the odds of improvement compared to ZDV+ddI.  Equivalently, ZDV+ddI
# has OR(Q) = 1/2.0 = 0.5 (halves improvement) — the benefit signal.
cal_target_or     <- 2.0
cal_k_grid_range  <- c(0, 3)
cal_grid_step     <- 0.05

# -- Simulation study ----------------------------------------------------------
sim_n_sample      <- 1000L
sim_n_noise       <- 0L

# -- Analysis flags ------------------------------------------------------------
run_fs            <- TRUE    # Run ForestSearch
run_fs_grf        <- FALSE   # Run FS with GRF pre-screening only
run_grf           <- TRUE    # Standalone GRF (grf.subg.harm.glm)

# -- ForestSearch parameters (benefit search thresholds) -----------------------
fs_or_threshold        <- round(1 / 0.60, 3)   # c1
fs_or_consistency      <- round(1 / 0.75, 3)   # c2
fs_pconsistency        <- 0.80
fs_splits              <- 1000L
fs_n_min               <- 60L
fs_d0_min              <- 10L
fs_d1_min              <- 10L
fs_maxk                <- 2L
fs_vi_grf_min          <- -0.2
fs_seedit              <- 8316951L
fs_cont_cutoff         <- 4L   # is.continuous() threshold (# unique values)

# -- FS-internal dmin.grf -----------------------------------------------------
# fs_dmin_grf is the dmin.grf value passed to forestsearch().  Inside
# forestsearch(), this parameter forwards to grf.subg.harm.glm() during
# the internal GRF candidate-cut extraction step (use_grf = TRUE).  The
# parameter MEANING is identical to the standalone GRF dmin.grf
# (minimum absolute CATE for a policy-tree node), but its ROLE differs:
#
#   - Standalone GRF  : dmin.grf is the FINAL subgroup-identification
#                       threshold.  Higher = stricter final subgroup.
#                       Controlled by grf_dmin (below).
#
#   - FS-internal GRF : dmin.grf is a CANDIDATE-CUT FILTER.  Cuts that
#                       fail this threshold are not passed back to FS's
#                       downstream enumeration.  Higher = fewer cuts
#                       reach FS, which may improve speed but can also
#                       remove cuts that FS would have used productively.
#                       Controlled by fs_dmin_grf (this variable).
#
# These two values are tuned independently.  The default 0.0 reproduces
# forestsearch()'s GLM default (any positive harm qualifies), so the
# existing simulation results are bit-identical.  Calibrate this
# independently from grf_dmin if you want a stricter pre-filter on FS
# candidate cuts.
fs_dmin_grf            <- 0.0

# -- Candidate-selection criterion (sg_focus) ---------------------------------
# `sg_focus` controls how forestsearch() sorts the candidate subgroups that
# meet the screening threshold, and therefore which one becomes the
# identified subgroup.  Five options (see ?subgroup_consistency):
#   "hr"       : primary sort = Pcons desc, secondary = effect size desc,
#                tertiary = K asc.  Package default.
#   "maxSG"    : primary sort = N desc (LARGEST candidate first),
#                secondary = Pcons desc, tertiary = K asc.  Use this when
#                the goal is to identify the LARGEST benefitting subgroup
#                among those meeting the consistency threshold.
#   "minSG"    : primary sort = N asc (smallest candidate first).
#   "hrMaxSG"  : compound (N desc, effect desc) — forces stop_threshold = NULL.
#   "hrMinSG"  : compound (N asc, effect desc) — forces stop_threshold = NULL.
#
# For this ACTG175 binary-benefit study we want to recover the LARGEST
# subgroup in which the ZDV+ddI combination is superior to ddI monotherapy,
# so we use "maxSG".  Early stopping is valid under "maxSG" (single sort
# criterion), though stop_threshold is set to NULL throughout this document.
fs_sg_focus            <- "maxSG"

# -- Continuous-variable cut strategy -----------------------------------------
# cut_type controls how candidate cuts are generated for each continuous
# covariate that forestsearch detects (i.e. any variable with more than
# fs_cont_cutoff unique values that is passed through confounders.name).
#
#   "default" : per continuous variable, get_conf_force() -> cut_var()
#               generates FOUR candidate cuts:
#                   var <= mean(var)
#                   var <= median(var)    (= Q2)
#                   var <= qlow(var)      (= Q1, 25th percentile)
#                   var <= qhigh(var)     (= Q3, 75th percentile)
#               This is the richer strategy and is the package default.
#
#   "median"  : per continuous variable, a SINGLE candidate cut:
#                   var <= median(var)
#               Use this to stress-test the "truly unknown cuts" regime
#               when the true cut is not at the median.
#
# Honest disclosure for this setup:
#   The true Q-defining cuts are age > 34 (~median of arms 1+3) and
#   preanti <= 744.5 (~Q3 of arms 1+3).  With cut_type = "default",
#   BOTH true cuts are present in the candidate set (age at median,
#   preanti at Q3).  With cut_type = "median", only the age cut is
#   recoverable; preanti's true Q3 cut is NOT in the candidate set,
#   forcing forestsearch to approximate Q via the wrong threshold.
#
# The default value ("default") is kept here so the simulation
# evaluates the realistic setting where the analyst uses the richer
# cut strategy a priori (without knowing the truth).  GRF candidate
# cuts (use_grf = TRUE) are additionally appended to this set.
fs_cut_type            <- "default"

# -- GRF standalone parameters ------------------------------------------------
# grf.subg.harm.glm() uses causal_forest() for candidate factor screening,
# then policy trees for subgroup identification.  With continuous inputs,
# policy trees automatically search over all candidate thresholds.
#
# dmin.grf: minimum absolute CATE (risk difference) for a policy-tree
#   node to qualify as a subgroup.  The calibration grids referenced
#   below were built on discretised inputs; with raw continuous inputs
#   the effective candidate-cut space is larger, which typically
#   INCREASES FPR slightly at a given dmin.grf.  Re-calibration is
#   recommended for production runs; dmin.grf = 0.10 is the current
#   conservative default carried over from the discretised setting.
grf_dmin               <- 0.1
grf_maxdepth           <- 2L
grf_sg_criterion       <- "mDiff"
grf_tune               <- FALSE

# -- ForestSearch pipeline flags -----------------------------------------------
fs_use_lasso           <- TRUE
fs_use_grf             <- TRUE
fs_is_rct              <- TRUE

# -- Single-inspection wrapper -------------------------------------------------
# fs_run() wraps forestsearch() with the parameter values defined above, so
# the two single-data / single-trial inspection calls (Sections 5 and 6) can
# share one definition instead of duplicating ~25 lines each.  The wrapper is
# intentionally narrow in scope: it is for interactive inspection runs where
# `details = TRUE` / `quiet = FALSE` are appropriate.  The simulation-loop
# path (Section 8) goes through run_simulation_analysis() instead, which
# constructs its own silent forestsearch() call internally.
#
# Arguments are the four column-name fields that differ between call sites;
# everything else (thresholds, pipeline flags, parallelism) is taken from
# the setup-chunk parameters.  Extra arguments are passed through to
# forestsearch() via `...` so a caller can override e.g. `maxk` without
# editing the wrapper.
fs_run <- function(data,
                   outcome_col,
                   event_col,
                   treat_col,
                   id_col = "id",
                   ...) {
  forestsearch(
    df.analysis      = data,
    confounders.name = confounders_analysis,
    outcome.name     = outcome_col,
    event.name       = event_col,
    treat.name       = treat_col,
    id.name          = id_col,
    outcome_type     = "binary",
    effect_measure   = "OR",
    seedit           = fs_seedit,
    n.min            = fs_n_min,
    d0.min           = fs_d0_min,
    d1.min           = fs_d1_min,
    hr.threshold     = fs_or_threshold,
    hr.consistency   = fs_or_consistency,
    pconsistency.threshold = fs_pconsistency,
    fs.splits        = fs_splits,
    max_subgroups_search = 15,
    maxk             = fs_maxk,
    sg_focus         = fs_sg_focus,
    use_lasso        = fs_use_lasso,
    use_grf          = fs_use_grf,
    is.RCT           = fs_is_rct,
    vi.grf.min       = fs_vi_grf_min,
    dmin.grf         = fs_dmin_grf,
    cont.cutoff      = fs_cont_cutoff,
    cut_type         = fs_cut_type,
    details          = TRUE,
    quiet            = FALSE,
    parallel_args    = list(plan = "sequential", workers = 1,
                             show_message = FALSE),
    ...
  )
}

# -- Reporting -----------------------------------------------------------------
sg_notation            <- "benefit"

# -- Output persistence --------------------------------------------------------
save_results           <- TRUE
output_dir             <- "../_data"

```

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

## Motivation

This document extends the ACTG175 benefit-search simulation
framework from survival outcomes (time-to-event) to a **binary
endpoint**: whether a patient's CD4 count improved from baseline
to 20 weeks.  The outcome is encoded on the **improvement scale**:
$y\_binary = I(\text{cd420} > \text{cd40})$, where a 1 indicates
**improvement**.  Combined with treatment switching
(ddI $\to$ `treat = 1`, ZDV+ddI $\to$ `treat = 0`),
$\text{OR} > c_1$ in the analysis means ddI increases the odds
of improvement in the identified subgroup — equivalently, ZDV+ddI
*harms* improvement there.  ForestSearch identifies this as a harm
subgroup; `subgroup_notation = "benefit"` relabels it for display.

A full reference table of effect-measure / outcome-direction
combinations appears in the [Appendix](#sec-appendix-conventions).
@sec-stat-goals summarises the row that applies to this vignette.

The simulation uses the `forestsearch` GLM simulation suite
(`generate_glm_dgm`, `calibrate_glm_interaction`,
`simulate_from_glm_dgm`) and routes through
`run_simulation_analysis()` via class-based dispatch on the
`"glm_dgm"` object.

## Realistic Analysis Setting

A prior version of this simulation discretised every continuous
covariate into a binary factor **before** handing the data to
`forestsearch()` / `grf.subg.harm.glm()`.  The binarisation used
the same cuts that define the true subgroup $Q$ (e.g. age > 34,
preanti $\leq$ 744.5).  That setup implicitly gives the analysis
method knowledge of the true cutpoints, which is unrealistic.

The current setup **retains continuous covariates in their raw
form for the analysis step**.  The data-generating mechanism
(DGM) is built from the discretised factors (`z1`--`z12`) because
`generate_glm_dgm()` requires factor covariates and the true
subgroup must be defined algebraically.  The analysis methods,
however, see the **raw** continuous columns (`age`, `preanti`,
`wtkg`, `karnof`, `cd40`, `cd80`) along with the six truly
binary indicators (`hemo`, `homo`, `drugs`, `race`, `gender`,
`symptom`).  Cutpoints for the continuous covariates are
discovered by the search methods themselves (median splits,
GRF-derived cuts, policy-tree splits), exactly as in a real
analysis.

::: {.callout-important}
## What changes vs the prior (discretised) setup

- **Ground truth is unchanged**: the true benefit subgroup $Q$
  is still $\{\text{age} > 34\} \cap \{\text{preanti} \leq 744.5\}$
  with prevalence $\approx 34\%$, and the DGM's OR(Q) calibration
  is untouched.
- **Classification metrics are unchanged in definition**: `flag_harm`
  is computed identically from `z1` and `z2`.
- **What changes is the search problem**: ForestSearch must
  discover the cuts from candidate thresholds; GRF builds policy
  trees over raw continuous inputs.  Expect lower sensitivity and
  PPV than the discretised setting, because the analyst does not
  receive oracle cuts.

**Cut-set coverage for this run.**  ForestSearch is configured with
`cut_type = "default"` (the package default), which generates four
candidate cuts per continuous covariate: mean, median, Q1, and Q3.
For the ACTG175 covariate distribution the median of `age` is
approximately 34 and Q3 of `preanti` is approximately 744.5, so
**both true Q-defining cuts happen to fall inside the default
candidate set** — they are simply not privileged over the other
candidates.  The analyst has no oracle knowledge of which cuts
matter; ForestSearch must select them based on the data.  Switching
to `cut_type = "median"` would exclude preanti's Q3 cut from the
candidate set entirely, providing a harder stress test.  GRF policy
trees search over all continuous thresholds internally and are
unaffected by this setting.
:::

## Statistical Goals {#sec-stat-goals}

This simulation study addresses three questions about
ForestSearch and GRF standalone subgroup identification
applied to **binary outcomes** in the realistic (raw covariate)
setting:

1. **Detection power (H1)**: When a benefit subgroup $Q$
   exists with $\text{OR}(Q) = `r cal_target_or`$ -- i.e., in
   $Q$, the experimental treatment (ZDV+ddI) doubles the odds
   of improvement compared to ddI -- how often do ForestSearch
   and GRF identify *any* subgroup?
2. **False positive control (H0)**: When the treatment effect
   is homogeneous (no true $Q$), how often does each method
   falsely declare a benefit subgroup?
3. **Classification accuracy (H1)**: Conditional on detection,
   how well does the estimated $\hat{Q}$ recover the true $Q$?
   Measured by sensitivity ($\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$: fraction of
   true $Q$ captured) and positive predictive value
   ($\text{ppv}(\hat{Q})$: fraction of $\hat{Q}$ truly in $Q$).

::: {.callout-note}
## Directional configuration for this vignette

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Outcome type | Binary |
| Native effect measure | OR |
| Y direction in the data | Improvement (`y_binary = 1` $\Leftrightarrow$ cd420 > cd40) |
| Search goal | Benefit (of ZDV+ddI) |
| Treatment coding | Switched (ddI = 1, ZDV+ddI = 0) |
| What "$\text{OR} > c_1$" means here | ddI increases P(improvement) in Q $\Leftrightarrow$ ZDV+ddI harms in Q |
| `subgroup_notation` | `"benefit"` |

This is one row of the Appendix master table
([@sec-appendix-conventions]) -- consult that table for any
other (outcome type $\times$ Y direction $\times$ search goal)
combination.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Summary of results
See [Summary] at the end for a data-driven
summary of detection, classification, and timing from this run.
:::

## Simulation Pipeline

The simulation proceeds in six steps:

1. **Data preparation** (@sec-data): Load the ACTG175 trial,
   restrict to arms 1 (ZDV+ddI) and 3 (ddI), switch treatment
   labels so ddI = `treat = 1` and ZDV+ddI = `treat = 0`
   (benefit search convention), and construct BOTH:
   (a) the binary `z1`--`z12` factor set needed by the DGM; and
   (b) the realistic analysis candidate set
   (`age`, `preanti`, `wtkg`, `karnof`, `cd40`, `cd80`, `hemo`,
   `homo`, `drugs`, `race`, `gender`, `symptom`).

2. **DGM construction** (@sec-dgm): Fit a logistic regression
   to the observed data using the `z1`--`z12` factor
   formulation, create a 5,000-subject super-population, and
   define the true benefit subgroup
   $Q = \{z_1 = 1 \cap z_2 = 1\}$ (age > `r actg_age_cut`
   AND preanti $\leq$ `r actg_preanti_cut`).  The super-
   population retains the **raw** covariate columns as well as
   the `z1`--`z12` indicators.

3. **Calibration** (@sec-calibrate): Search over `k_inter`
   values to find the interaction strength that produces
   $\text{OR}(Q) = `r cal_target_or`$ -- a 2$\times$ odds-ratio
   of improvement for the experimental treatment in $Q$ (see
   @sec-stat-goals for the directional convention).

4. **Single-data analysis** (@sec-single): Run ForestSearch
   and GRF on the observed ACTG175 data using the **raw**
   analysis candidate set to verify the pipeline produces
   valid results before scaling to simulation.

5. **Monte Carlo simulation** (@sec-sims): For each of
   `r nsims_alt` alternative and `r nsims_null` null
   replicates, draw a random sample of $N = `r sim_n_sample`$
   from the DGM super-population, run ForestSearch and GRF
   on the raw analysis covariates, and record detection,
   classification, and effect estimates.

6. **Evaluation** (@sec-results): Compute operating
   characteristics (detection, sensitivity, PPV, effect
   estimation bias) under both hypotheses.

## Benefit Search on the OR Scale

The benefit-search approach from Leon et al. (2024, Section 4.2)
applies identically to binary outcomes, with odds ratios (OR)
replacing hazard ratios (HR).  The full configuration is shown in
the directional table in @sec-stat-goals and in the master
reference table in @sec-appendix-conventions; in brief, the
combination of switched treatment and adverse-coded `y_binary`
makes the package's harm-search machinery point at the benefit
direction, with screening threshold $c_1 =$ `r fs_or_threshold`
and consistency threshold $c_2 =$ `r fs_or_consistency` (both
sourced from the Quarto setup chunk).  Inversion to the original
scale is handled automatically by the package when
`subgroup_notation = "benefit"` is passed to the reporting
functions.


## Candidate Selection: `sg_focus = "maxSG"`

When several candidate subgroups simultaneously meet both the screening
threshold ($c_1 =$ `r fs_or_threshold`) and the consistency threshold
($c_2 =$ `r fs_or_consistency`), `forestsearch()` must pick one.  That
choice is governed by `sg_focus`.  Five options are available:

| `sg_focus`  | Primary sort   | Secondary        | Interpretation |
|-------------|----------------|------------------|----------------|
| `"hr"`      | Pcons      | effect       | Package default. Favours *most-consistent* candidate. |
| `"maxSG"`   | **N **     | Pcons        | **Largest** qualifying candidate. |
| `"minSG"`   | N           | Pcons        | Smallest qualifying candidate. |
| `"hrMaxSG"` | N          | effect       | Compound. Forces `stop_threshold = NULL`. |
| `"hrMinSG"` | N         | effect       | Compound. Forces `stop_threshold = NULL`. |

For the ACTG175 benefit search, the analytic goal is to recover the
**largest subgroup in which the ZDV+ddI combination is superior to ddI
monotherapy** — the population we would, in a real trial, most want to
describe and quantify.  Once the screening-plus-consistency filter has
passed, there is no further reason to pick a smaller, tighter subgroup;
the largest qualifying candidate is the most policy-relevant one.

We therefore use `fs_sg_focus <- "maxSG"` throughout this document (set
in the Quarto setup chunk). The concrete effect is:

- **Sort is by candidate N (descending)**, with Pcons as tiebreaker.
  Among candidates that pass screening and consistency, FS keeps the
  one with the largest $|H|$.
- **Single sort criterion**, so early stopping remains valid;
  `stop_threshold` can still be set if desired.  (In this document we
  set `stop_threshold = NULL` so all qualifying candidates are
  enumerated.)

This choice has two practical consequences that we track throughout
the operating-characteristics analysis:

1. $\widehat{|H|}$ will typically be closer to $|Q|$ than under the
   default `sg_focus = "hr"`, which trades size for consistency and
   tends to return strict subsets of $Q$.
2. The distribution of identified subgroups across simulations
   (reported in Section 8.2) should concentrate on a small number of
   definitions close to the true $Q$ anchor, rather than fragmenting
   into many small tight splits.


# GRF Standalone: Calibration Notes {#sec-grf-calibration}

The standalone GRF analysis uses `grf.subg.harm.glm()` with
`causal_forest()` for candidate variable screening and policy
trees for subgroup identification.  The key tuning parameter
is `dmin.grf`, the minimum absolute CATE (conditional average
treatment effect) on the **risk difference** scale required for
a policy-tree node to be valid.

## Configuration

For the **benefit + positive** scenario with switched treatment
(the ACTG175 binary configuration), the correct GRF setup is:

- `adverse_outcome = FALSE` (Y = improvement is positive)
- Treatment indicator = **switched** (ddI = 1, ZDV+ddI = 0)
- GRF identifies the subgroup where the switched "treatment"
  produces the most negative CATE --- i.e., where ddI monotherapy
  is worst relative to combination, which is the **benefit**
  subgroup on the original scale.

## Impact of Raw Continuous Inputs on Calibration

Prior `dmin.grf` calibration (in `grf_dmin_calibration_binary.qmd`)
was conducted on **discretised** inputs (`z1`--`z12` binary
factors) and recommended `dmin.grf = 0.02` for the benefit +
positive binary configuration.

With raw continuous inputs the policy-tree search evaluates
many more candidate thresholds per covariate, which tends to:

- **Widen the null distribution of the best CATE**, inflating
  the false positive rate at a given `dmin.grf`.
- **Improve sensitivity to the true cuts** when they align with
  natural splits in the covariate distribution.

The current document uses `dmin.grf = `r grf_dmin`` as a
conservative default carried over from the discretised setting.
A dedicated calibration run with raw continuous inputs is
recommended before production scaling.

::: {.callout-note}
The GRF FPR is higher than ForestSearch's because GRF lacks the
bootstrap consistency filter.  ForestSearch requires the subgroup
effect to exceed a threshold in 90% of bootstrap replicates,
providing stronger FPR control at the cost of lower detection.
The two methods are complementary: GRF provides a
threshold-free comparison.
:::


# Data Preparation {#sec-data}

```{r load-packages}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Library loads (click to expand)"
library(forestsearch)
library(survival)
library(speff2trial)
library(data.table)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(doFuture)
library(foreach)

# Safe foreach result collection and worker resets are provided by
# forestsearch v0.2.0 via the exported helpers collect_results() and
# reset_workers() (R/forestsearch_helpers.R).  Call as
# forestsearch::collect_results(...) or just collect_results(...) after
# library(forestsearch).
```

```{r prepare-datasets}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Data preparation (click to expand)"

t0 <- proc.time()[3]

# -- ACTG175: arms 1 (ZDV+ddI) vs 3 (ddI) ------------------------------------
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% actg_arms)
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Original treatment: arm 1 = 1, arm 3 = 0
actg_df$treat_orig <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == actg_treat_arm, 1L, 0L)

# Switched treatment for benefit search
actg_df$treat <- 1L - actg_df$treat_orig

# -- Binary outcome: CD4 response at 20 weeks ---------------------------------
# Improvement scale: y_binary = 1 when the patient's CD4 count improved
# (cd420 > cd40).  With switched treatment (ddI = 1), OR > c1 in Q means
# ddI increases the odds of improvement — ForestSearch identifies this as
# the "harm" subgroup; subgroup_notation = "benefit" relabels for display.
actg_df$y_binary <- as.integer(actg_df$cd420 > actg_df$cd40)

# Remove subjects with missing cd420
n_before <- nrow(actg_df)
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]
n_after  <- nrow(actg_df)

# =============================================================================
# Two parallel covariate views are constructed on the SAME data frame:
#
#   (1) DGM factor set: z1--z12 binary factors. Used by generate_glm_dgm()
#       and calibrate_glm_interaction() to fit the baseline logistic
#       regression and define the TRUE subgroup Q = {z1=1 & z2=1}.
#
#   (2) Analysis candidate set: raw continuous covariates + truly binary
#       indicators. Used by forestsearch() and grf.subg.harm.glm() in
#       both the observed-data analysis and every simulated replicate.
#       The analyst does NOT know the cuts that define Q.
# =============================================================================

# -- (1) DGM factor set: z1-z12 binary factors --------------------------------
#
# The z-series preserves the discretisation from León et al. (2024,
# Section 4.2). These are needed by the DGM because generate_glm_dgm()
# requires factor covariates, and because the true Q is defined
# algebraically in terms of z1 and z2.
actg_df$z1  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$age > actg_age_cut, 1L, 0L))
actg_df$z2  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$preanti <= actg_preanti_cut, 1L, 0L))
actg_df$z3  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$wtkg <= 75, 1L, 0L))
actg_df$z4  <- as.factor(ifelse(
  actg_df$karnof <= median(actg_df$karnof), 1L, 0L))
actg_df$z5  <- as.factor(ifelse(
  actg_df$cd40 <= median(actg_df$cd40), 1L, 0L))
actg_df$z6  <- as.factor(ifelse(
  actg_df$cd80 <= median(actg_df$cd80), 1L, 0L))
actg_df$z7  <- as.factor(actg_df$hemo)
actg_df$z8  <- as.factor(actg_df$homo)
actg_df$z9  <- as.factor(actg_df$drugs)
actg_df$z10 <- as.factor(actg_df$race)
actg_df$z11 <- as.factor(actg_df$gender)
actg_df$z12 <- as.factor(actg_df$symptom)

# -- (2) Analysis candidate set: raw + binary ---------------------------------
#
# The continuous columns (age, preanti, wtkg, karnof, cd40, cd80) are
# ALREADY in the ACTG175 dataframe in their raw form. We make the six
# truly-binary indicators into factors so that forestsearch's
# is.continuous() detection treats them as categorical without
# attempting median/GRF cuts.
for (v in analysis_binary_vars) {
  actg_df[[v]] <- as.factor(actg_df[[v]])
}

confounders_analysis <- c(analysis_continuous_vars, analysis_binary_vars)

# Sanity: covariate-type inventory for the analyst-visible candidate set
cov_types <- vapply(confounders_analysis,
  function(v) if (is.factor(actg_df[[v]])) "factor" else class(actg_df[[v]])[1],
  character(1))
n_unique_per_cov <- vapply(confounders_analysis,
  function(v) length(unique(actg_df[[v]])), integer(1))

# -- True subgroup flag (for reference; generate_glm_dgm creates its own) -----
actg_df$flag_harm_ref <- as.integer(
  actg_df$z1 == 1 & actg_df$z2 == 1
)

# -- Summary scalars captured for downstream display ---------------------------
# y_binary = improvement: mean(y_binary) is the improvement rate directly.
n_ex_missing <- n_before - n_after
resp_overall <- 100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary)
resp_ZDV_ddI <- 100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat_orig == 1])
resp_ddI     <- 100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat_orig == 0])
Q_n          <- sum(actg_df$flag_harm_ref)
Q_N          <- nrow(actg_df)
Q_prev_pct   <- 100 * mean(actg_df$flag_harm_ref)

# Response-rate 2x2 grid (row = subgroup, col = treatment arm)
resp_grid <- data.frame(
  Subgroup  = c("Q (age > 34 & preanti \u2264 745)",
                "Qc (complement)"),
  `ZDV+ddI` = c(
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$flag_harm_ref == 1 & actg_df$treat_orig == 1]),
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$flag_harm_ref == 0 & actg_df$treat_orig == 1])),
  `ddI`     = c(
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$flag_harm_ref == 1 & actg_df$treat_orig == 0]),
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$flag_harm_ref == 0 & actg_df$treat_orig == 0])),
  check.names = FALSE
)

timings$data_prep <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```

::: {.callout-note title="Dataset summary"}
- **Source cohort**: ACTG175 arms 1 (ZDV+ddI, experimental) and 3
  (ddI, control). N = `r n_before` before exclusion,
  **N = `r Q_N`** after removing `r n_ex_missing` subject(s) with
  missing `cd420`.
- **Outcome**: binary response,
  `y_binary = I(cd420 > cd40)` (improvement scale).
  Overall **improvement** rate `r sprintf("%.1f%%", resp_overall)`;
  ZDV+ddI arm `r sprintf("%.1f%%", resp_ZDV_ddI)`; ddI arm
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", resp_ddI)`.
- **True subgroup Q** (used for ground-truth classification only, not
  exposed to the analysis methods): age $>$ `r actg_age_cut` AND
  preanti $\le$ `r actg_preanti_cut`. Prevalence **`r Q_n` / `r Q_N`
  (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", Q_prev_pct)`)**.
- **Analysis candidate set** (`r length(confounders_analysis)` covariates):
  `r length(analysis_continuous_vars)` continuous
  (`r paste(analysis_continuous_vars, collapse = ", ")`) +
  `r length(analysis_binary_vars)` binary factors
  (`r paste(analysis_binary_vars, collapse = ", ")`).
- **DGM factor set**: z1–z12 binary factors, preserving the
  discretisation from León et al. (2024, Section 4.2). Kept on the same
  data frame so `generate_glm_dgm()` can build the super-population from
  the factor representation while the analysis methods see the raw
  continuous covariates.
:::

)

gt::gt(resp_grid) |>

      cal_target_or))

# Creating the Binary DGM {#sec-dgm}

The GLM DGM uses `generate_glm_dgm()` to fit a logistic regression
on the observed ACTG175 data, create a super-population with
individual-level potential outcomes ($p_0$, $p_1$), and compute
true subgroup effects.  `calibrate_glm_interaction()` then searches
for the `k_inter` that produces the target OR(Q).

**Note on DGM inputs.**  The DGM continues to use the `z1`--`z12`
factor formulation.  This is a design requirement of
`generate_glm_dgm()` (which coerces any input to `factor` via
`as.factor()`) and is also the natural way to define the true
subgroup $Q$ algebraically.  The super-population returned by
the DGM *retains all original columns of `actg_df`*, including
the raw `age`, `preanti`, `wtkg`, `karnof`, `cd40`, `cd80`
columns, which are then used by the analysis step.

## Step 1: Build Initial DGM

```{r create-dgm-alt}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

dgm_alt_init <- generate_glm_dgm(
  data          = actg_df,
  factor_vars   = dgm_factor_vars,
  outcome_var   = "y_binary",
  treatment_var = "treat",
  outcome_type  = "binary",
  effect_measure = "OR",
  subgroup_vars = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  model         = "alt",
  k_treat       = dgm_k_treat_alt,
  k_inter       = 0,    # no interaction before calibration
  n_super       = dgm_n_super,
  seed          = sim_seed,
  verbose       = TRUE
)

cat("\n=== Initial ACTG175 Binary DGM ===\n")
cat("  OR(Q):  ", round(dgm_alt_init$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, 3), "\n")
cat("  OR(Qc): ", round(dgm_alt_init$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup, 3), "\n")
cat("  OR(ITT):", round(dgm_alt_init$hazard_ratios$overall, 3), "\n")

# Sanity check: super-population retains raw continuous columns
missing_raw <- setdiff(analysis_continuous_vars, names(dgm_alt_init$df_super))
if (length(missing_raw) > 0) {
  stop("DGM super-population is missing raw continuous columns: ",
       paste(missing_raw, collapse = ", "))
} else {
  cat("\nRaw continuous columns present in super-population: ",
      paste(analysis_continuous_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

timings$dgm_init <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```

## Step 2: Calibrate for Target OR {#sec-calibrate}

### Why calibrate?

The DGM's `k_inter` parameter controls the strength of the
treatment-by-subgroup interaction on the log-odds scale.  Because
the mapping from `k_inter` to the marginal OR(Q) is non-linear and
depends on the covariate distribution and baseline response rates,
we search over a grid of candidate values.

`calibrate_glm_interaction()` automates this process: it evaluates
`generate_glm_dgm()` at each grid point and selects the `k_inter`
closest to the target.

```{r calibrate}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

dgm_calibrated <- calibrate_glm_interaction(
  data            = actg_df,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  outcome_var     = "y_binary",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  target_effect   = cal_target_or,
  outcome_type    = "binary",
  effect_measure  = "OR",
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  k_treat         = dgm_k_treat_alt,
  k_inter_range   = cal_k_grid_range,
  grid_step       = cal_grid_step,
  n_super         = dgm_n_super,
  seed            = sim_seed,
  verbose         = TRUE
)

cat("\n=== Calibrated ACTG175 Binary DGM ===\n")
cat("  OR(Q):  ", round(dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, 3),
    " (target:", cal_target_or, ")\n")
cat("  OR(Qc): ", round(dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup, 3), "\n")
cat("  OR(ITT):", round(dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$overall, 3), "\n")
cat("  k_inter:", dgm_calibrated$model_params$k_inter, "\n")
cat("  -> Original scale: OR(Q) =",
    round(1 / dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, 3), "\n")

timings$calibrate <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```

### Calibration Curve

```{r calibration-plot, fig.height=5}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Calibration-curve ggplot (click to expand)"
#| fig-cap: "Calibration of k_inter: OR(Q) on the improvement scale as a function of the interaction parameter."

cal_grid <- seq(cal_k_grid_range[1], cal_k_grid_range[2], by = cal_grid_step)
cal_or_Q <- vapply(cal_grid, function(k) {
  d <- generate_glm_dgm(
    data = actg_df, factor_vars = dgm_factor_vars,
    outcome_var = "y_binary", treatment_var = "treat",
    outcome_type = "binary", subgroup_vars = dgm_subgroup_vars,
    subgroup_cuts = dgm_subgroup_cuts, model = "alt",
    k_treat = dgm_k_treat_alt,
    k_inter = k, n_super = dgm_n_super, seed = sim_seed
  )
  d$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup
}, numeric(1))

cal_df <- data.frame(k_inter = cal_grid, or_Q = cal_or_Q)
best_k <- dgm_calibrated$model_params$k_inter
or_Q_cal <- dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup

ggplot(cal_df, aes(x = k_inter, y = or_Q)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cal_target_or, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.0, linetype = "dotted",
             colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(
    data = data.frame(k_inter = best_k, or_Q = or_Q_cal),
    colour = "red", size = 4, shape = 16
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "k_inter",
    y = "OR(Q), switched scale",
    title = "ACTG175 Binary DGM Calibration",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Best: k_inter = %.2f -> OR(Q) = %.3f (target: %.1f)",
      best_k, or_Q_cal, cal_target_or
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```


### Illustrative `k_treat` values: OR(ITT), OR(Q), and gap to c1

To give the reader a concrete sense of how `k_treat` shifts the
marginal and subgroup effects under H1, the table below holds the
calibrated `k_inter` fixed and varies `k_treat` over the same grid
$\{0.5, 1.0, 1.5\}$ as the null analog.  `k_treat` scales the
fitted main treatment effect directly, so $\text{OR}(\text{ITT})$
tracks `k_treat` smoothly; $\text{OR}(Q)$ inherits both the
scaled main effect and the held-fixed interaction, so it hits
the calibration target $\text{OR}(Q) = `r cal_target_or`$ only at
the calibration `k_treat` and drifts away as `k_treat` is
perturbed.  **Larger** `k_treat` amplifies the main effect,
pushing both $\text{OR}(\text{ITT})$ and $\text{OR}(Q)$ further
above c1 (improving FS detection); **smaller** `k_treat`
attenuates and may pull $\text{OR}(Q)$ back toward c1
(degrading detection).

```{r dgm-alt-illustrate}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Build three illustrative alt DGMs and tabulate (click to expand)"

# Three illustrative alt DGMs.  k_inter is HELD FIXED at the value
# returned by calibration (dgm_calibrated$model_params$k_inter); only
# k_treat varies.  These DGMs are NOT used in the simulation loop
# below — the simulation uses dgm_calibrated, which is the calibrated
# alt DGM at k_treat = dgm_k_treat_alt.  The grid here is purely a
# didactic table.
k_inter_cal  <- dgm_calibrated$model_params$k_inter
k_treat_grid <- c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5)

illust_rows_alt <- lapply(k_treat_grid, function(k) {
  d <- generate_glm_dgm(
    data           = actg_df,
    factor_vars    = dgm_factor_vars,
    outcome_var    = "y_binary",
    treatment_var  = "treat",
    outcome_type   = "binary",
    effect_measure = "OR",
    subgroup_vars  = dgm_subgroup_vars,
    subgroup_cuts  = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
    model          = "alt",
    k_treat        = k,
    k_inter        = k_inter_cal,
    n_super        = dgm_n_super,
    seed           = sim_seed,
    verbose        = FALSE
  )
  or_ITT_switched <- as.numeric(d$hazard_ratios$overall)
  or_Q_switched   <- as.numeric(d$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup)
  data.frame(
    k_treat       = k,
    or_itt_switch = or_ITT_switched,
    or_itt_orig   = 1 / or_ITT_switched,
    or_Q_switch   = or_Q_switched,
    or_Q_orig     = 1 / or_Q_switched,
    gap_to_c1     = fs_or_threshold - or_Q_switched
  )
})
illust_tbl_alt <- do.call(rbind, illust_rows_alt)

gt::gt(illust_tbl_alt) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title    = "Illustrative alt DGMs: OR(ITT), OR(Q), and gap to c1 by k_treat",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      paste0("ACTG175 benefit search, switched scale; ",
             "c1 = %.3f, k_inter = %.3f (held fixed), n_super = %d"),
      fs_or_threshold, k_inter_cal, dgm_n_super
    )
  ) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(
    label   = "OR(ITT)",
    columns = c(or_itt_switch, or_itt_orig)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(
    label   = "OR(Q)",
    columns = c(or_Q_switch, or_Q_orig)
  ) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    k_treat       = "k_treat",
    or_itt_switch = "switched",
    or_itt_orig   = "original",
    or_Q_switch   = "switched",
    or_Q_orig     = "original",
    gap_to_c1     = gt::md("Gap (c1 \u2212 OR_Q_switched)")
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns  = c(or_itt_switch, or_itt_orig,
                 or_Q_switch,   or_Q_orig,   gap_to_c1),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = k_treat, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style    = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(rows = k_treat == 1.0)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_footnote(
    footnote = paste0(
      "k_treat = 1.0 (bold row) preserves the fitted main treatment ",
      "effect; this is the function default for generate_glm_dgm(). ",
      "This document's calibration was performed at k_treat = ",
      format(dgm_k_treat_alt, nsmall = 1),
      " (set in the setup chunk via dgm_k_treat_alt), and the resulting ",
      "k_inter = ", sprintf("%.3f", k_inter_cal),
      " is held fixed across all three rows.  k_treat scales the main ",
      "treatment effect directly, so OR(ITT) tracks k_treat smoothly; ",
      "OR(Q) hits the calibration target only at the calibration k_treat ",
      "because the held-fixed k_inter still adds to the linear predictor ",
      "for Q members regardless of k_treat. ",
      "Note: under H1, a NEGATIVE gap (last column) means OR(Q) exceeds ",
      "c1, which is detection-favorable -- the opposite sign convention ",
      "from the null table (where a positive gap is favorable, i.e., no ",
      "false alarm). Effects are computed exactly from the super-",
      "population's individual potential outcomes (p0, p1); marginal ORs ",
      "depend on the covariate distribution and are not, in general, ",
      "equal to any single conditional OR."
    )
  )
```


## Step 3: Create Null DGM

Under `model = "null"`, the treatment effect is **homogeneous**
across all patients (no treatment effect heterogeneity).
Per León et al. (2024, Section 3), $Q = \emptyset$ and
$Q^c$ is the ITT population.  The `flag_harm` column is
retained as a structural label in the simulated data (marking
$z_1 = 1 \cap z_2 = 1$) but has **no treatment-effect
meaning**: there is no true benefit subgroup under this
hypothesis.

```{r dgm-null}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

dgm_null <- generate_glm_dgm(
  data          = actg_df,
  factor_vars   = dgm_factor_vars,
  outcome_var   = "y_binary",
  treatment_var = "treat",
  outcome_type  = "binary",
  subgroup_vars = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  model         = "null",
  k_treat       = dgm_k_treat_null,
  n_super       = dgm_n_super,
  seed          = sim_seed,
  verbose       = TRUE
)

cat("\n=== ACTG175 Null DGM ===\n")
cat("  OR(ITT):", round(dgm_null$hazard_ratios$overall, 3), "\n")
cat("  OR(Q):  ", round(dgm_null$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, 3), "\n")
cat("  OR(Qc): ", round(dgm_null$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup, 3), "\n")

timings$dgm_null <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```


### Illustrative `k_treat` values: OR(ITT) and gap to c1

To give the reader a concrete sense of how `k_treat` controls the
marginal ITT effect and therefore the gap from c1, the table below
constructs three illustrative null DGMs at `k_treat` $\in \{0.5,
1.0, 1.5\}$ using the same data, factor list, super-population
size, and seed as the main `dgm_null` above.  The default
(`k_treat = 1.0`) preserves the fitted ITT effect; **larger**
`k_treat` amplifies the marginal benefit, pushing the
switched-scale OR further above 1 and *narrowing* the gap to c1;
**smaller** `k_treat` attenuates the marginal effect toward
OR $\approx 1$ and *widens* the gap.

```{r dgm-null-illustrate}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Build three illustrative null DGMs and tabulate (click to expand)"

# Three illustrative null DGMs.  These are NOT used in the simulation
# loop below; the simulation uses `dgm_null` from the previous chunk
# (constructed with k_treat = dgm_k_treat_null).  The grid here is
# purely a didactic table so the reader can see how k_treat moves
# OR(ITT) and the gap to c1.
k_treat_grid <- c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5)

illust_rows <- lapply(k_treat_grid, function(k) {
  d <- generate_glm_dgm(
    data           = actg_df,
    factor_vars    = dgm_factor_vars,
    outcome_var    = "y_binary",
    treatment_var  = "treat",
    outcome_type   = "binary",
    effect_measure = "OR",
    subgroup_vars  = dgm_subgroup_vars,
    subgroup_cuts  = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
    model          = "null",
    k_treat        = k,
    n_super        = dgm_n_super,
    seed           = sim_seed,
    verbose        = FALSE
  )
  or_switched <- as.numeric(d$hazard_ratios$overall)
  data.frame(
    k_treat     = k,
    or_switched = or_switched,
    or_original = 1 / or_switched,
    gap_to_c1   = fs_or_threshold - or_switched
  )
})
illust_tbl <- do.call(rbind, illust_rows)

gt::gt(illust_tbl) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title    = "Illustrative null DGMs: OR(ITT) and gap to c1 by k_treat",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "ACTG175 benefit search, switched scale; c1 = %.3f, n_super = %d",
      fs_or_threshold, dgm_n_super
    )
  ) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    k_treat     = "k_treat",
    or_switched = "OR(ITT, switched)",
    or_original = "OR(ITT, original)",
    gap_to_c1   = gt::md("Gap (c1 \u2212 OR_switched)")
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns  = c(or_switched, or_original, gap_to_c1),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = k_treat, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style    = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(rows = k_treat == 1.0)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_footnote(
    footnote = paste0(
      "k_treat = 1.0 (bold row) preserves the fitted ITT effect; this is ",
      "the function default for generate_glm_dgm(). This document's null ",
      "simulation uses k_treat = ", format(dgm_k_treat_null, nsmall = 1),
      " (set in the setup chunk via dgm_k_treat_null). Smaller k_treat ",
      "attenuates the marginal effect toward OR \u2248 1 (widening the gap ",
      "to c1); larger k_treat amplifies the effect (narrowing the gap). ",
      "The realised OR is computed exactly from the super-population's ",
      "individual potential outcomes (p0, p1); the marginal OR depends ",
      "on the covariate distribution and is not, in general, equal to ",
      "any single conditional OR."
    )
  )
```


# Single-Data Analysis {#sec-single}

:::{.callout-important title="Real-data setting: no ground-truth classification"}
This section analyses the **actual ACTG175 data** -- not a simulated
trial.  The true benefit subgroup in a real trial is **unknown**; it is
the object the analysis is trying to estimate.  We therefore report the
subgroup ForestSearch identifies and the resulting arm-specific ORs,
but we **do not** compute classification metrics (sens / spec / PPV)
against any reference subgroup -- there is no clinical truth to
classify against.  Classification is only meaningful in the simulation
setting of @sec-sims, where the DGM fixes a known $Q$.
:::

Before any simulation, run ForestSearch on the **actual ACTG175
data** with `details = TRUE` to examine every step of the
procedure: LASSO screening, GRF variable importance, candidate
enumeration, and bootstrap consistency.

The analysis uses the **realistic candidate set**:

```{r show-analysis-set}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Echo candidate covariate set (click to expand)"
#| output: false
cat("Analysis candidate covariates (no oracle cuts):\n")
cat("  Continuous:", paste(analysis_continuous_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("  Binary:    ", paste(analysis_binary_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("\nForestsearch / GRF will discover cuts on the continuous\n")
cat("covariates themselves; the TRUE cuts (age > 34, preanti <= 745)\n")
cat("are NOT provided.\n")
```

::: {.callout-note title="What the analysis methods see"}
The analysis candidate set (passed to `forestsearch()` / `grf.subg.harm.glm()`
as `confounders.name`) is:

- **Continuous** (`r length(analysis_continuous_vars)`):
  `r paste(analysis_continuous_vars, collapse = ", ")`
- **Binary** (`r length(analysis_binary_vars)`):
  `r paste(analysis_binary_vars, collapse = ", ")`

The methods discover cuts on the continuous covariates themselves;
the TRUE cuts (age $>$ `r actg_age_cut`, preanti $\le$
`r actg_preanti_cut`) are **not** provided.
:::

```{r single-data}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "fs_run() on real data (click to expand)"
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

# ForestSearch on ACTG175 observed data
#   outcome_type = 'binary', effect_measure = 'OR'
#   Treatment: switched (ddI = 1, ZDV+ddI = 0)
#   Y = I(cd420 > cd40) = improvement
#   Covariates: RAW continuous + binary indicators
#   Thresholds: c1 = fs_or_threshold, c2 = fs_or_consistency

fs_actg <- fs_run(
  data        = actg_df,
  outcome_col = "y_binary",
  event_col   = "y_binary",
  treat_col   = "treat",
  id_col      = "id"
)

timings$single_data <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```

## Examine Result

```{r examine-single}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Examine FS result + subgroup OR fits (click to expand)"

cat("\n=== ForestSearch Result ===\n")

if (!is.null(fs_actg$grp.consistency)) {
  # NOTE: for a forestsearch object, the cut expressions defining the
  # identified subgroup live in `grp.consistency$sg.harm` (character
  # vector of factor-level cut names).  `grp.consistency$sg.harm.id`
  # is a different object: a per-subject 0/1 indicator of subgroup
  # membership with length nrow(df).  (For GRF objects, `sg.harm.id`
  # does carry the cut expressions — same name, different semantics.)
  sg <- fs_actg$grp.consistency$sg.harm
  if (!is.null(sg) && length(sg) > 0 && !all(is.na(sg))) {
    cat("Subgroup identified:", paste(sg, collapse = " & "), "\n")

    df_est <- fs_actg$df.est
    in_H  <- df_est$treat.recommend == 0
    in_Hc <- df_est$treat.recommend == 1

    cat(sprintf("  Size(H): %d,  Size(Hc): %d\n",
        sum(in_H), sum(in_Hc)))

    if (sum(in_H) >= 10) {
      fit_H <- glm(y_binary ~ treat, data = df_est[in_H, ],
                    family = binomial)
      or_H <- exp(coef(fit_H)["treat"])
      cat(sprintf("  OR(H):  %.3f\n", or_H))
    }
    if (sum(in_Hc) >= 10) {
      fit_Hc <- glm(y_binary ~ treat, data = df_est[in_Hc, ],
                     family = binomial)
      or_Hc <- exp(coef(fit_Hc)["treat"])
      cat(sprintf("  OR(Hc): %.3f\n", or_Hc))
    }

    fit_itt <- glm(y_binary ~ treat, data = df_est, family = binomial)
    cat(sprintf("  OR(ITT): %.3f\n",
        exp(coef(fit_itt)["treat"])))
  } else {
    cat("No subgroup identified by ForestSearch.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("ForestSearch did not return grp.consistency.\n")
}

cat(sprintf("\nSingle-data analysis: %.1f sec\n", timings$single_data))
```

## GRF Standalone on Observed Data

```{r grf-single-data}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "GRF standalone call + output (click to expand)"

grf_actg <- grf.subg.harm.glm(
  data             = actg_df,
  confounders.name = confounders_analysis,
  outcome.name     = "y_binary",
  treat.name       = "treat",
  id.name          = "id",
  outcome_type     = "binary",
  effect_measure   = "OR",
  dmin.grf         = grf_dmin,
  maxdepth         = grf_maxdepth,
  RCT              = TRUE,
  sg.criterion     = grf_sg_criterion,
  details          = TRUE
)

if (!is.null(grf_actg$sg.harm.id) && length(grf_actg$sg.harm.id) > 0) {
  cat("GRF subgroup:", paste(grf_actg$sg.harm.id, collapse = " & "), "\n")
  grf_H <- grf_actg$data$treat.recommend == 0
  cat(sprintf("  Size(H): %d,  Size(Hc): %d\n",
      sum(grf_H), sum(!grf_H)))
} else {
  cat("GRF: no subgroup identified.\n")
}
```


## FS vs GRF Concordance on Observed Data

When a method does not detect a subgroup, its classification is
"all subjects to $Q^c$" (`treat.recommend = 1` for everyone).
`compare_fs_subgroups()` handles this automatically — no manual
fallback is needed.

```{r fs-grf-concordance}
sg_compare <- compare_fs_subgroups(
  fs1                = fs_actg,
  fs2                = grf_actg,
  label1             = "ForestSearch",
  label2             = "GRF Standalone",
  id.name            = "id",
  subgroup_notation  = sg_notation,
  title              = "FS vs GRF: Subgroup Membership Concordance",
  subtitle           = "ACTG175 observed data (binary benefit search, raw continuous)",
  font_size          = 13
)

sg_compare$table
```

```{r fs-grf-concordance-detail}
cat("Concordance statistics:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Agreement: %.1f%%\n",
    100 * sg_compare$concordance$agreement))
cat(sprintf("  Cohen's kappa: %.3f\n",
    sg_compare$concordance$kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Concordant: %d / Discordant: %d / Total: %d\n",
    sg_compare$concordance$n_agree,
    sg_compare$concordance$n_disagree,
    sg_compare$concordance$n_total))
```


# Single Trial Simulation {#sec-single-trial}

Before the full simulation study, simulate a **single replicate** from
the calibrated DGM and run the two analysis methods end-to-end with
`details = TRUE`.  This mirrors what every replicate inside the Monte
Carlo loop will see and lets us sanity-check the full pipeline --
LASSO screening, GRF pre-screening, candidate enumeration, consistency
evaluation, subgroup-effect estimation -- before burning the budget of
thousands of replicates.

Unlike @sec-single, the **true subgroup here is known by construction**
(it is the DGM-embedded Q).  Per-replicate classification metrics are
reported in aggregate for the full simulation loop in @sec-results;
here we show only the identified subgroup definitions and estimated
ORs so the pipeline can be inspected end-to-end on a single replicate.

```{r single-trial-simulate}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Simulate one trial from the calibrated DGM (click to expand)"
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

# ── Simulate one trial from the calibrated DGM ─────────────────────────
df_single <- simulate_from_glm_dgm(
  dgm  = dgm_calibrated,
  n    = sim_n_sample,
  seed = sim_seed + 1L
)

cat(sprintf("Single trial: N = %d, response rate = %.1f%%\n",
    nrow(df_single), 100 * mean(df_single$y_sim)))
cat(sprintf("  treat allocation: %.1f%%\n",
    100 * mean(df_single$treat_sim)))
cat(sprintf("  True Q prevalence: %.1f%%\n",
    100 * mean(df_single$flag_harm)))

# ── Verify OR in the simulated data ───────────────────────────────────
fit_single <- glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim, data = df_single, family = binomial)
cat(sprintf("  Simulated ITT OR: %.3f (DGM target: %.3f)\n",
    exp(coef(fit_single)["treat_sim"]),
    dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$overall))

# ── Confirm raw continuous columns are present in simulated data ──────
missing_in_sim <- setdiff(confounders_analysis, names(df_single))
if (length(missing_in_sim) > 0) {
  stop("Simulated data is missing analysis columns: ",
       paste(missing_in_sim, collapse = ", "))
}
```

## ForestSearch on the Simulated Trial

```{r single-trial-fs}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "fs_run() on the simulated trial (click to expand)"

# Ensure a stable id column for compare_fs_subgroups() alignment
df_single$id <- seq_len(nrow(df_single))

fs_single <- fs_run(
  data        = df_single,
  outcome_col = "y_sim",
  event_col   = "y_sim",
  treat_col   = "treat_sim",
  id_col      = "id"
)
```

```{r single-trial-fs-summary}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Examine FS result on simulated trial (click to expand)"

cat("\n=== ForestSearch on simulated trial ===\n")

if (!is.null(fs_single$sg.harm) && length(fs_single$sg.harm) > 0L &&
    !all(is.na(fs_single$sg.harm))) {

  cat("Subgroup identified (cut expressions):\n")
  for (s in fs_single$sg.harm) cat("  ", s, "\n")

  df_est <- fs_single$df.est
  in_H   <- df_est$treat.recommend == 0

  # Subgroup effect on switched and original scales
  if (sum(in_H) >= 10L) {
    fit_H <- glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim,
                 data = df_est[in_H, ], family = binomial)
    or_H  <- exp(coef(fit_H)["treat_sim"])
    cat(sprintf("\n  OR(H_hat, switched) = %.3f  (inverted: %.3f)\n",
        or_H, 1/or_H))
  }
  if (sum(!in_H) >= 10L) {
    fit_Hc <- glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim,
                  data = df_est[!in_H, ], family = binomial)
    cat(sprintf("  OR(Hc_hat, switched) = %.3f  (inverted: %.3f)\n",
        exp(coef(fit_Hc)["treat_sim"]),
        1/exp(coef(fit_Hc)["treat_sim"])))
  }

} else {
  cat("No subgroup identified by ForestSearch on this replicate.\n")
}
```

## GRF Standalone on the Simulated Trial

```{r single-trial-grf}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "GRF call + output on simulated trial (click to expand)"

grf_single <- grf.subg.harm.glm(
  data             = df_single,
  confounders.name = confounders_analysis,
  outcome.name     = "y_sim",
  treat.name       = "treat_sim",
  id.name          = "id",
  outcome_type     = "binary",
  effect_measure   = "OR",
  dmin.grf         = grf_dmin,
  maxdepth         = grf_maxdepth,
  RCT              = TRUE,
  sg.criterion     = grf_sg_criterion,
  details          = TRUE
)

cat("\n=== GRF standalone on simulated trial ===\n")
if (!is.null(grf_single$sg.harm.id) &&
    length(grf_single$sg.harm.id) > 0L &&
    !all(is.na(grf_single$sg.harm.id))) {
  cat("GRF subgroup (cut expressions):\n")
  for (s in grf_single$sg.harm.id) cat("  ", s, "\n")

  grf_H  <- grf_single$data$treat.recommend == 0
  cat(sprintf("  Size(H): %d,  Size(Hc): %d\n",
      sum(grf_H), sum(!grf_H)))
} else {
  cat("GRF: no subgroup identified on this replicate.\n")
}

timings$single_trial <- proc.time()[3] - t0
cat(sprintf("\nSingle trial analysis: %.1f sec\n", timings$single_trial))
```

# Running Simulation Studies {#sec-sims}

## Setup

```{r sim-setup}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "FS / GRF parameter lists for run_simulation_analysis() (click to expand)"

plan(multisession, workers = n_workers)
cat("Using", n_workers, "parallel workers\n")

# -- Candidate variable set (RAW continuous + binary) --------------------------
# This is the key behavioural change vs the prior discretised setup:
# forestsearch() and grf.subg.harm.glm() receive raw continuous inputs
# and must discover cuts.
cat("Analysis confounders passed to FS/GRF:\n")
cat("  ", paste(confounders_analysis, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# -- ForestSearch parameters ---------------------------------------------------
fs_params <- list(
  # Column name mappings
  outcome.name           = "y_sim",
  event.name             = "y_sim",
  treat.name             = "treat_sim",
  id.name                = "id",

  # GLM pipeline
  outcome_type           = "binary",
  effect_measure         = "OR",

  # Variable screening
  use_lasso              = fs_use_lasso,
  use_grf                = fs_use_grf,

  # Consistency algorithm (v0.2.0 default: 3-10x speedup)
  use_twostage           = TRUE,

  # Continuous-variable detection threshold
  cont.cutoff            = fs_cont_cutoff,

  # Candidate cut strategy for continuous covariates
  # ("default" = mean + median + Q1 + Q3 per continuous variable;
  #  "median"  = median only). See setup chunk for full explanation.
  cut_type               = fs_cut_type,

  # Subgroup detection thresholds
  # Note: hr.threshold/hr.consistency are the generic ForestSearch
  # parameter names regardless of endpoint type. For binary outcomes,
  # these represent OR thresholds on the switched scale.
  hr.threshold           = fs_or_threshold,
  hr.consistency         = fs_or_consistency,
  pconsistency.threshold = fs_pconsistency,

  # Candidate-selection criterion: "maxSG" prefers the LARGEST
  # candidate subgroup meeting the consistency threshold (see setup
  # chunk for full description of sg_focus options).
  sg_focus               = fs_sg_focus,

  # Computational constraints
  fs.splits              = fs_splits,
  n.min                  = fs_n_min,
  d0.min                 = fs_d0_min,
  d1.min                 = fs_d1_min,
  maxk                   = fs_maxk,
  vi.grf.min             = fs_vi_grf_min,
  dmin.grf               = fs_dmin_grf,   # FS-internal GRF cut filter
  seedit                 = fs_seedit,

  # GRF tuning (applies to ForestSearch's internal GRF pre-screening)
  tune_grf               = grf_tune,

  # Inner parallelism: sequential within each worker
  parallel_args          = list(
    plan = "sequential", workers = 1, show_message = FALSE
  )
)

# -- GRF standalone parameter overrides ----------------------------------------
grf_params <- list(
  dmin.grf     = grf_dmin,
  maxdepth     = grf_maxdepth,
  sg.criterion = grf_sg_criterion,
  tune_grf     = grf_tune
)
```


## Alternative Hypothesis Simulations

```{r run-alt}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "H1 simulation loop — foreach wiring + run_simulation_analysis() (click to expand)"
#| output: false
cat("Running", nsims_alt, "simulations under H1...\n")
if (diag_keep_first_n > 0L) {
  cat(sprintf("  Diagnostic capture: keep = {%s}, first %d sim(s)\n",
      paste(diag_keep, collapse = ", "), diag_keep_first_n))
}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

results_alt_raw <- foreach(
  sim = seq_len(nsims_alt),
  .errorhandling = "pass",
  .options.future = list(
    packages = c("forestsearch", "survival", "data.table", "future"),
    seed = TRUE
  )
) %dofuture% {
  future::plan("sequential")
  run_simulation_analysis(
    sim_id           = sim,
    dgm              = dgm_calibrated,
    n_sample         = sim_n_sample,
    confounders_base = confounders_analysis,
    n_add_noise      = sim_n_noise,
    run_fs           = run_fs,
    run_fs_grf       = run_fs_grf,
    run_grf          = run_grf,
    fs_params        = fs_params,
    grf_params       = grf_params,
    keep             = diag_keep,
    keep_first_n     = diag_keep_first_n,
    verbose          = FALSE
  )
}

timings$sims_alt <- proc.time()[3] - t0

# Post-hoc failure accounting + diagnostic harvest
# keep_diagnostics = TRUE preserves per-replicate fs_full / candidate_table
# attached by run_simulation_analysis() (stripped by rbindlist otherwise).
results_alt <- collect_results(results_alt_raw, "H1 alt",
                               keep_diagnostics = diag_keep_first_n > 0L)
n_failed_alt <- attr(results_alt, "n_failed")
diagnostics_alt <- attr(results_alt, "diagnostics")

cat("Completed in", round(timings$sims_alt / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
cat("Results:", nrow(results_alt), "rows\n")
if (n_failed_alt > 0) cat(sprintf("  *** %d FAILED ***\n", n_failed_alt))
if (!is.null(diagnostics_alt))
  cat(sprintf("  Diagnostic objects captured: %d replicate(s)\n",
      length(diagnostics_alt)))
if (nrow(results_alt) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("Detection rate: %.1f%%\n",
      100 * mean(results_alt$any.H[results_alt$analysis == "FS"])))
} else {
  cat("All simulations failed — see error messages above.\n")
  cat("Common causes:\n")
  cat("  1. devtools::document() -> devtools::install() -> restart R needed\n")
  cat("  2. Package version mismatch between interactive and worker sessions\n")
}
```


## ForestSearch Sensitivity Diagnostic {#sec-fs-sensitivity}

:::{.callout-note title="Why this section exists"}
Empirically, FS sensitivity in this configuration hovers around 20%.
That raises the question: **which subgroups is FS actually
identifying?**  If it consistently picks up one component of the true
subgroup $Q = \{\text{age} > 34 \cap \text{preanti} \le 745\}$ but
misses the other, the low sensitivity is mechanical (one-of-two cuts
→ ≈ 50% true-Q overlap, further diluted by cut-point mismatch).  If
it picks noise variables, the low sensitivity reflects a different
problem.  The diagnostics below separate these hypotheses.
:::

### Per-replicate subgroup definitions (first 20)

The `sg.def` column on `results_alt` carries the cut-expression string
of the FS-identified subgroup for **every** replicate (a v0.2.0
addition to `run_simulation_analysis()`).  We print the first 20
alongside the corresponding sensitivity / PPV / size for context.

```{r fs-diag-per-sim}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "First N FS subgroup definitions (click to expand)"

fs_rows <- results_alt[results_alt$analysis == "FS", ]
show_n  <- min(20L, nrow(fs_rows))

diag_tbl <- data.frame(
  sim      = fs_rows$sim[seq_len(show_n)],
  any.H    = fs_rows$any.H[seq_len(show_n)],
  size.H   = fs_rows$size.H[seq_len(show_n)],
  sens     = round(fs_rows$sens[seq_len(show_n)], 3),
  ppv      = round(fs_rows$ppv[seq_len(show_n)],  3),
  sg.def   = fs_rows$sg.def[seq_len(show_n)],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

diag_tbl$sg.def[!nzchar(diag_tbl$sg.def)] <- "(none identified)"

knitr::kable(
  diag_tbl,
  col.names = c("Sim", "any.H", "|H_hat|", "Sens", "PPV",
                "Identified subgroup"),
  caption = sprintf(
    "First %d H1 replicates: FS-identified subgroup definitions.",
    show_n),
  align = c("r", "c", "r", "r", "r", "l")
)
```

### Cross-replicate subgroup-definition frequency (all sims)

```{r fs-diag-def-freq}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Cross-replicate subgroup-definition frequency (click to expand)"

all_defs <- fs_rows$sg.def
all_defs[!nzchar(all_defs)] <- "(none identified)"

def_freq <- sort(table(all_defs), decreasing = TRUE)
def_df <- data.frame(
  subgroup = names(def_freq),
  n        = as.integer(def_freq),
  pct      = round(100 * as.integer(def_freq) / length(all_defs), 1),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Show all unique subgroups (usually <= 20) or top 20
show_rows <- min(20L, nrow(def_df))
knitr::kable(
  def_df[seq_len(show_rows), ],
  col.names = c("Identified subgroup",
                "Replicates",
                "% of H1 sims"),
  caption = sprintf(
    "Frequency of FS-identified subgroup definitions across %d H1 replicates.",
    length(all_defs)),
  row.names = FALSE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r")
)
```

### Variable-level frequency

Each subgroup definition is a conjunction of one or more cut
expressions.  Here we parse out the **variable names** appearing in
those cuts and count how often each variable is selected.  If FS is
recovering one component of true-$Q$ but missing the other, this
table will show a strong imbalance between `age` and `preanti`.

```{r fs-diag-var-freq}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Variable-level frequency across FS finds (click to expand)"

extract_vars <- function(sg_str) {
  if (!nzchar(sg_str)) return(character(0))
  parts <- strsplit(sg_str, "\\s*&\\s*", perl = TRUE)[[1]]
  # A cut expression may be wrapped in braces and optionally negated:
  #   "{age <= 34}"       -> variable "age"
  #   "!{age <= 34}"      -> variable "age"
  #   "preanti"           -> variable "preanti"   (plain indicator)
  # Strip the outer !/{ / } wrappers, then take the first whitespace-
  # delimited token — the variable name.
  vars <- vapply(parts, function(p) {
    p <- trimws(p)
    p <- sub("^!", "",  p)           # optional negation
    p <- sub("^\\{", "", p)           # optional opening brace
    p <- sub("\\}$", "", p)           # optional closing brace
    tok <- strsplit(trimws(p), "\\s+", perl = TRUE)[[1]][1]
    if (is.na(tok)) "" else tok
  }, character(1))
  unique(vars[nzchar(vars)])
}

all_var_uses <- unlist(lapply(fs_rows$sg.def, extract_vars))
if (length(all_var_uses) == 0L) {
  cat("No identified subgroups across any replicate.\n")
} else {
  var_freq <- sort(table(all_var_uses), decreasing = TRUE)
  n_detect <- sum(nzchar(fs_rows$sg.def))
  var_df <- data.frame(
    variable       = names(var_freq),
    n_times_used   = as.integer(var_freq),
    pct_of_detects = round(100 * as.integer(var_freq) / n_detect, 1),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  knitr::kable(
    var_df,
    col.names = c("Variable",
                  "Times used",
                  "% of detecting sims"),
    caption = sprintf(
      paste0("Variables appearing in FS-identified subgroups across ",
             "%d detecting replicates (of %d total)."),
      n_detect, nrow(fs_rows)),
    row.names = FALSE,
    align = c("l", "r", "r")
  )
}
```

### FS-pipeline diagnostic columns

These columns (populated by `run_simulation_analysis()` from the full
`forestsearch()` result per replicate) let us check whether FS is
completing the full search or exiting via early stopping, and how
many candidates it's evaluating.

```{r fs-diag-pipeline}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "FS diagnostic columns (click to expand)"

if ("n_candidates_evaluated" %in% names(fs_rows)) {
  pipe_df <- data.frame(
    metric = c("Pconsistency threshold met (n_passed > 0)",
               "Early stopping triggered",
               "Candidates evaluated (mean)",
               "Candidates total available (mean)",
               "FS runtime, minutes (mean)"),
    value  = c(
      sprintf("%.1f%% of sims",
              100 * mean(fs_rows$n_passed > 0, na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%.1f%% of sims",
              100 * mean(fs_rows$early_stop_triggered, na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%.1f",
              mean(fs_rows$n_candidates_evaluated, na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%.1f",
              mean(fs_rows$n_candidates_total, na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%.2f",
              mean(fs_rows$fs_minutes, na.rm = TRUE))
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  knitr::kable(
    pipe_df,
    col.names = c("Diagnostic", "Value"),
    caption = "FS pipeline diagnostics aggregated across H1 replicates.",
    align = c("l", "r")
  )
}
```

### Full `fs_full` objects for the first few sims (if captured)

When `diag_keep_first_n > 0` and `"fs_full" %in% diag_keep`, the full
`forestsearch()` result objects (minus `df.est`/`df.predict` to keep
memory bounded) are attached as `attr(results_alt, "diagnostics")`,
keyed by `sim_id`.  Below we pull the first one and inspect the
candidate-evaluation table — which lists every subgroup that passed
the screening threshold and their consistency p-values.

```{r fs-diag-candidate-peek}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Peek at full fs_full objects for first few sims (click to expand)"

if (!is.null(diagnostics_alt) && length(diagnostics_alt) > 0L) {
  # diagnostics_alt is named by sim_id: $sim1 / $sim2 / ...
  first_key <- names(diagnostics_alt)[1L]
  d <- diagnostics_alt[[first_key]]

  cat(sprintf("Captured diagnostics for %d replicate(s): %s ... %s\n",
      length(diagnostics_alt),
      utils::head(names(diagnostics_alt), 1L),
      utils::tail(names(diagnostics_alt), 1L)))
  cat(sprintf("\nInspecting keeper set for '%s':\n", first_key))
  cat("  methods:", paste(names(d), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  if (!is.null(d$FS)) {
    cat("  FS keepers: ", paste(names(d$FS), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }

  # Show the FS candidate table for the first captured replicate
  if (!is.null(d$FS$candidate_table) &&
      inherits(d$FS$candidate_table, "data.frame") &&
      nrow(d$FS$candidate_table) > 0L) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "\nCandidate subgroups evaluated for %s (top 10 by row):\n",
      first_key))
    print(utils::head(d$FS$candidate_table, 10L))
  }
} else {
  cat("No diagnostics captured (diag_keep_first_n == 0 or all sims failed).\n")
}
```

### Interpretation

Read the four tables above top-to-bottom:

- If the **subgroup-definition frequency** shows a handful of
  recurring cut expressions dominating, FS is converging on a small
  number of candidates.  If one of them matches true-$Q$ closely
  (e.g., `age <= 34 & preanti <= 745`), sensitivity on those sims
  should be high in the per-sim table.
- If the **variable frequency** shows `age` dominating and `preanti`
  rarely present (or vice versa), FS is recovering **one component
  only**.  Sensitivity of ≈ 0.50 on that sub-population of sims is
  expected; weighted by the fraction of times both are found, the
  average lands near 20%.  This is a candidate-enumeration issue,
  not a pathology.
- If noise variables (`noise1`, …) show up prominently, the threshold
  or consistency settings are too permissive for this sample size.
- If `n_passed > 0` is low (say < 30%), the identification threshold
  `fs_or_threshold` is binding and the subgroup is being **rejected
  outright** in most sims.  This would show up as `size.H = 0` and
  `any.H = 0L` for those replicates in the per-sim table.

The combination of the four tables is enough to pick between these
hypotheses without re-running anything.




```{r reset-workers-null}
# Reset worker pool between alt and null phases to prevent memory
# accumulation and worker bloat (null sims on bloated workers can be
# ~20x slower).  reset_workers() is exported from forestsearch v0.2.0.
forestsearch::reset_workers(workers = n_workers)
```

```{r run-null}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "H0 simulation loop (click to expand)"
#| output: false
cat("Running", nsims_null, "simulations under H0...\n")
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

results_null_raw <- foreach(
  sim = seq_len(nsims_null),
  .errorhandling = "pass",
  .options.future = list(
    packages = c("forestsearch", "survival", "data.table", "future"),
    seed = TRUE
  )
) %dofuture% {
  future::plan("sequential")
  run_simulation_analysis(
    sim_id           = sim,
    dgm              = dgm_null,
    n_sample         = sim_n_sample,
    confounders_base = confounders_analysis,

}

timings$sims_null <- proc.time()[3] - t0

results_null <- collect_results(results_null_raw, "H0 null")
n_failed_null <- attr(results_null, "n_failed")

cat("Completed in", round(timings$sims_null / 60, 1), "minutes\n")

    100 * mean(results_null$any.H[results_null$analysis == "FS"])))
```
