# Results {#sec-results}

## Metrics Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Classification metrics follow the definitions in León et al.
(2024, Section 3) adapted for the benefit search.

### Detection

**Found** ($\text{any}(Q)$): proportion of simulations where
the method identifies *any* benefit subgroup
($\texttt{any.H} = 1$).

- **Under H1** (alternative): $Q$ exists with a differential
  treatment effect.  $\text{any}(Q)$ is **detection power**.
- **Under H0** (null): $Q = \emptyset$ and $Q^c$ is the ITT
  population.  $\text{any}(Q)$ is the **false positive rate
  (FPR)** for falsely declaring that a benefit subgroup exists.

### Classification Under H1

Under the alternative, the true benefit subgroup $Q$ exists
($Q = \{z_1 = 1 \cap z_2 = 1\}$, prevalence $\approx 34\%$)
with a genuinely different treatment effect.  Following
León et al. (2024, Section 3), define for estimated
subgroup $\hat{Q}$:

$$
\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in Q\}},
\quad
\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in \hat{Q}\}},
$$

with analogous measures for the complement $\hat{Q}^c$.

The operating-characteristics tables report these as:

| Table column | León et al. notation | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| **Sen** | $\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$ | Fraction of true $Q$ captured by $\hat{Q}$ |
| **Spec** | $\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c)$ | Fraction of true $Q^c$ correctly in $\hat{Q}^c$ |
| **PPV** | $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q})$ | Fraction of $\hat{Q}$ truly in $Q$ |
| **NPV** | $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c)$ | Fraction of $\hat{Q}^c$ truly in $Q^c$ |

Classification metrics are averaged across **all** simulations
(León et al. 2024, Table 1).  When no subgroup is detected
($\hat{Q} = \emptyset$), the simulation contributes
$\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = 0$ and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = 0$
(since no member of $Q$ is captured and no subjects are
assigned to $\hat{Q}$).  This convention is implemented
at the source in `run_simulation_analysis()`, matching
the original `fs.estimates.out()` function used in
León et al. (2024).

::: {.callout-note}
## Classification metrics with discovered cuts

Because cuts are discovered from the data in this setup, a
$\hat{Q}$ that captures "roughly the right region" but with
slightly shifted boundaries will still receive high sens/PPV.
Expect these metrics to be lower than under the discretised
(oracle-cut) setup — the gap quantifies the cost of not knowing
the true cuts in advance.
:::

### Classification Under H0

Under the null, $Q = \emptyset$ --- no subgroup with a
differential treatment effect exists.  The complement $Q^c$
is the entire ITT population.  Per León et al. (2024,
Section 3), $\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$ is **undefined** (shown
as "—" in the table) and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) \equiv 0$.
For the complement, $\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c) = |\hat{Q}^c|/N$
and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c) = 1$ since $Q^c$ = ITT.

The only operationally meaningful metric under H0 is the
**detection rate (FPR)**.

### Effect Estimates

All effect estimates are displayed on the **original** treatment
scale (OR $< 1$ = benefit from ZDV+ddI) via
`subgroup_notation = "benefit"`.

## Operating Characteristics Under H1

```{r oc-alt}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

format_oc_results(
  results_alt,
  metrics   = c("detection", "classification", "subgroup_size"),
  digits    = 2,
  digits_hr = 2,
  title     = "ACTG175 Binary: Identification (Benefit Search, Raw Continuous)",
  subtitle  = sprintf(
    "n = %d, %d sims, OR(Q) = %.2f, OR(Qc) = %.2f (switched scale)",
    sim_n_sample, nsims_alt,
    dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup,
    dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup
  ),
  subgroup_notation = sg_notation
)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Interpreting high Sens / low PPV"}
The combination of high sensitivity (~85%) with low specificity (~20%)
and low PPV (~35%) is internally consistent and follows directly from
Bayes' theorem.  The Bayes relationship is:

$$
\text{PPV}
= \frac{\text{Sens} \times \pi}
       {\text{Sens} \times \pi + (1 - \text{Spec}) \times (1 - \pi)}
$$

where $\pi \approx 34\%$ is the true-$Q$ prevalence.  Substituting the
observed metrics confirms PPV $\approx$ 35%.  The pattern arises because
$\hat{Q}$ is **much larger than $Q$** --- roughly 2--2.5$\times$ the
true subgroup size (check avg$|\hat Q|$ above).  The method recovers
most of $Q$ (high sensitivity) but also absorbs most of $Q^c$ (low
specificity), yielding a "diluted" $\hat{Q}$ with low purity (PPV).
This is expected when cuts are discovered from continuous covariates
rather than known *a priori*; the raw-continuous boundary
$\{z_1 = 1 \cap z_2 = 1\}$ is harder to recover precisely than a
discretised oracle-cut design.
:::

### True Subgroup Sizes Across Replicates

`run_simulation_analysis()` records the per-replicate size of the
**true** benefit subgroup $Q$ (`flag_harm == 1`) and its complement
$Q^c$ (`flag_harm == 0`) in the columns `sizeH_true`, `sizeHc_true`,
`propH_true`, `propHc_true`.  The estimation tables below report
$\widehat{|H|}$ (the identified subgroup size averaged across
replicates); the callout here gives the corresponding true-subgroup
sizes for comparison.

```{r true-size-summary}
#| code-fold: true

# One row per replicate-method combination, but sizeH_true is identical
# across method rows within the same sim. Deduplicate on sim.
truth_by_sim <- unique(results_alt[, c("sim", "sizeH_true", "sizeHc_true",
                                        "propH_true", "propHc_true")])

callout_Q <- sprintf(
  "|Q|:  mean = %.1f (SD %.2f),  range = [%d, %d],  prop = %.1f%%",
  mean(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  sd(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  min(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  max(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true),
  100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propH_true))

callout_Qc <- sprintf(
  "|Qc|: mean = %.1f (SD %.2f),  range = [%d, %d],  prop = %.1f%%",
  mean(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  sd(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  min(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  max(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true),
  100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propHc_true))

cat(sprintf("True subgroup sizes across %d H1 replicates (N = %d each):\n",
            nrow(truth_by_sim), sim_n_sample))
cat("  ", callout_Q,  "\n")
cat("  ", callout_Qc, "\n")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Reference sizes for the estimation tables below"}
- **|Q| (true benefit subgroup)**: mean `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true))`
  per trial (SD `r sprintf("%.2f", sd(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true))`,
  range `r min(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true)`–`r max(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true)`,
  average proportion `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propH_true))`).
- **|Qc| (complement)**: mean `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true))`
  per trial (SD `r sprintf("%.2f", sd(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true))`,
  range `r min(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true)`–`r max(truth_by_sim$sizeHc_true)`,
  average proportion `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propHc_true))`).

Compare to $\widehat{|H|}$ (the FS-identified subgroup size) reported in
the row-group labels of the estimation tables below.  A ratio
$\widehat{|H|} \big/ \overline{|Q|} \approx 1$ indicates the method is
recovering a subgroup close to the true size; values much smaller
suggest FS is identifying a strict subset of $Q$; values larger suggest
FS is absorbing some $Q^c$ subjects into $\hat H$.
:::

### Distribution of Identified Subgroups

::: {.callout-tip title="Reminder: the true subgroup"}
The true subgroup $Q$ that FS is trying to recover is defined by
$\{\text{age} > `r actg_age_cut`\} \cap
 \{\text{preanti} \le `r actg_preanti_cut`\}$.

- **Observed ACTG175 prevalence**: `r Q_n` / `r Q_N`
  (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", Q_prev_pct)`).
- **Simulated-trial prevalence** ($n = `r sim_n_sample`$): mean
  `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true))` (SD
  `r sprintf("%.2f", sd(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true))`,
  range `r min(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true)`–`r max(truth_by_sim$sizeH_true)`,
  proportion `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(truth_by_sim$propH_true))`).

Under H1 the bar chart should concentrate on definitions close to this
anchor.  Under H0 the true subgroup does not exist, so any finds
reflect false discovery across the candidate space.
:::

The distribution of the identified subgroup $\hat H$ under H1
(calibrated HTE) and H0 (null) is rendered by
`forestsearch::plot_sg_distribution()`.  Three vignette-level settings
control how the charts behave:

1. **Top-K cap** (`sgdist_top_k` = `r sgdist_top_k`): at most that
   many bars are shown; additional passing labels pool into a single
   "Other (*k* labels)" row (or are suppressed -- see
   `sgdist_show_other_alt` / `sgdist_show_other_null`).  Without
   this, a diffuse H0 with one find per distinct label (the textbook
   false-positive signature) renders as overlapping, unreadable
   rows.
2. **Auto-halving** (`max_halvings = 2L`): the minimum-percentage
   thresholds (`sgdist_min_pct_alt` = `r sgdist_min_pct_alt`%,
   `sgdist_min_pct_null` = `r sgdist_min_pct_null`%) are halved up
   to twice if no label clears the initial value, so the chart does
   not render empty.
3. **Adaptive figure height** via `sgdist_fig_height()`, driven by
   `attr(p, "n_bars")`, keeps the vertical resolution consistent
   across scenarios regardless of how many distinct labels pass the
   filter.

```{r oc-sgdist-build}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Build subgroup-distribution plots (click to expand)"

plot_sgdist_alt <- plot_sg_distribution(
  results              = results_alt[results_alt$analysis == "FS", ],
  any_col              = "any.H",
  label_col            = "sg.def",
  min_pct              = sgdist_min_pct_alt,
  top_k                = sgdist_top_k,
  show_other           = sgdist_show_other_alt,
  max_halvings         = 2L,
  bar_label_inside     = TRUE,
  placeholder_on_empty = TRUE,
  title                = "HTE: Subgroups Identified (H-hat)",
  wrap_width           = 30
)

plot_sgdist_null <- plot_sg_distribution(
  results              = results_null[results_null$analysis == "FS", ],
  any_col              = "any.H",
  label_col            = "sg.def",
  min_pct              = sgdist_min_pct_null,
  top_k                = sgdist_top_k,
  show_other           = sgdist_show_other_null,
  max_halvings         = 2L,
  bar_label_inside     = TRUE,
  placeholder_on_empty = TRUE,
  title                = "Null: Subgroups Identified (H-hat)",
  wrap_width           = 30
)

h_alt  <- sgdist_fig_height(attr(plot_sgdist_alt,  "n_bars"))
h_null <- sgdist_fig_height(attr(plot_sgdist_null, "n_bars"))
```

```{r oc-alt-sgdist, fig.width=10, fig.height=h_alt}
#| code-fold: true

print(plot_sgdist_alt)
```

```{r oc-null-sgdist, fig.width=10, fig.height=h_null}
#| code-fold: true

print(plot_sgdist_null)
```

Under `sg_focus = "maxSG"` and H1, the chart should concentrate on
definitions close to the true $Q$ anchor (age $> 34$ and preanti
$\le$ 745 on the discretised side of the DGM).  Under H0 the find
rate is low and any bars that clear the (possibly auto-halved)
threshold are scattered across the candidate space — the expected
false-discovery signature.  When the H0 chart is dominated by a large
"Other (*k* labels)" bar — i.e., many distinct labels each passing
the threshold at count 1 or 2 — that is itself the diagnostic: FS is
firing on unrelated noise with no preferred label.

### Distribution of Effect Estimates

The MRCT analogue is `forestsearch::SGplot_estimates()`, which
displays violins for four populations (ITT, non-AP training, AP
testing, AP-subgroup) defined by the train/test split used in the
MRCT consistency framework.  The ACTG175 binary-benefit study is a
single-population design (no train/test split), so we construct a
three-panel binary analogue using the columns `hr.itt` (ITT OR),
`hr.H.hat` (identified subgroup $\hat H$), and `hr.Hc.hat`
(identified complement $\hat H^c$) that `run_simulation_analysis()`
already populates.  All three are on the switched-treatment scale
and inverted to the original benefit scale for display.  On the
benefit scale, OR $> 1$ indicates the ZDV+ddI combination is superior
to ddI monotherapy.  As before, both H1 and H0 scenarios are shown.

```{r oc-alt-ordist, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "H1 OR-distribution violin (click to expand)"

or_Q_true <- 1 / dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup

plot_effect_distribution(
  results           = results_alt,
  analysis_method   = "FS",
  effect_measure    = "OR",
  subgroup_notation = sg_notation,
  reference_effect  = or_Q_true,
  ylim              = ordist_ylim,
  title             = "ACTG175 Binary (HTE): OR Estimates Across Simulations",
  subtitle          = sprintf(
    "n = %d, %d sims | dotted green = true OR(Q) on benefit scale = %.2f",
    sim_n_sample, nsims_alt, or_Q_true)
)
```

```{r oc-null-ordist, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "H0 OR-distribution violin (click to expand)"

# Under H0 the DGM has no benefit subgroup -- no true-effect reference.
plot_effect_distribution(
  results           = results_null,
  analysis_method   = "FS",
  effect_measure    = "OR",
  subgroup_notation = sg_notation,
  ylim              = ordist_ylim,
  title             = "ACTG175 Binary (Null): OR Estimates Across Simulations",
  subtitle          = sprintf(
    "n = %d, %d sims | no true harm/benefit subgroup; dashed red = OR = 1",
    sim_n_sample, nsims_null)
)
```

Under H1 (top panel), the left violin (ITT) is centred near the DGM's
implied ITT benefit; the middle violin ($\widehat{\mathrm{OR}}(\hat
H)$) should concentrate near the dotted green reference line at the
true $\mathrm{OR}(Q)$; the right violin ($\widehat{\mathrm{OR}}(\hat
H^c)$) shows the residual effect in the complement and should sit
near $\mathrm{OR} = 1$ (i.e., no benefit in $\hat H^c$ once $\hat H$
is removed).  Under H0 (bottom panel), all three violins should
centre near $\mathrm{OR} = 1$; any concentration away from 1 in the
subgroup panels, conditional on a subgroup being found, reflects the
selection-driven bias that the bootstrap bias-correction in
`forestsearch()` is designed to correct.

```{r oc-alt-tables}
build_estimation_table(
  results         = results_alt,
  dgm             = dgm_calibrated,
  analysis_method = "FS",
  subtitle = sprintf(
    "ACTG175 Binary DGM (raw cont.) | n = %d, %d sims",
    sim_n_sample, nsims_alt
  ),
  font_size = 16,
  subgroup_notation = sg_notation
)

if ("GRF" %in% unique(results_alt$analysis)) {
  build_estimation_table(
    results         = results_alt,
    dgm             = dgm_calibrated,
    analysis_method = "GRF",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "ACTG175 Binary DGM, GRF raw cont. (dmin=%.2f) | n = %d, %d sims",
      grf_dmin, sim_n_sample, nsims_alt
    ),
    font_size = 16,
    subgroup_notation = sg_notation
  )
}

timings$report_alt <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```

### Projection for Production Runs

```{r projection}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Projection arithmetic (click to expand)"
#| results: asis

# Per-replicate cost (simulation loop only)
time_per_alt  <- timings$sims_alt / nsims_alt
time_per_null <- timings$sims_null / nsims_null

# prod_alt and prod_null defined in setup chunk
proj_alt  <- time_per_alt * prod_alt
proj_null <- time_per_null * prod_null
proj_other <- timings$total - timings$sims_alt - timings$sims_null
proj_total <- proj_alt + proj_null + proj_other

proj_df <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    sprintf("Current run (%d alt + %d null on %d workers)",
            nsims_alt, nsims_null, n_workers),
    "Per-replicate, H1",
    "Per-replicate, H0",
    sprintf("Projected H1 (%d sims)", prod_alt),
    sprintf("Projected H0 (%d sims)", prod_null),
    "Projected other (calibration, setup, reporting)",
    "Projected total"),
  Seconds = c(NA_real_,
              time_per_alt, time_per_null,
              proj_alt, proj_null, proj_other, proj_total),
  Minutes = c(NA_real_,
              time_per_alt / 60, time_per_null / 60,
              proj_alt / 60, proj_null / 60, proj_other / 60,
              proj_total / 60),
  Hours   = c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_,
              NA_real_, proj_total / 3600),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

cat(gt::as_raw_html(
  gt::gt(proj_df) |>
    gt::tab_header(title = sprintf(
      "Projected runtime for production simulation (%d H1 + %d H0)",
      prod_alt, prod_null)) |>
    gt::fmt_number(columns = c("Seconds", "Minutes", "Hours"),
                   decimals = 1) |>
    gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "\u2014") |>
    gt::cols_label(Metric  = gt::md("**Metric**"),
                   Seconds = gt::md("**Seconds**"),
                   Minutes = gt::md("**Minutes**"),
                   Hours   = gt::md("**Hours**")) |>
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = 11)
), "\n\n")
```


# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## Key Differences from the Survival Simulation

This document mirrors the structure of `actg175_simulations_benefit.qmd`
(survival endpoint) with the following differences:

1. **No censoring**: the binary outcome $I(\text{cd420} > \text{cd40})$
   is fully observed, eliminating censoring model complexity.

2. **Package GLM simulation suite**: uses `generate_glm_dgm()`,
   `calibrate_glm_interaction()`, and `simulate_from_glm_dgm()`
   instead of `generate_aft_dgm_flex()`, manual grid search, and
   `simulate_from_dgm()`.  `run_simulation_analysis()` dispatches
   automatically based on the `"glm_dgm"` class.

3. **OR replaces HR**: thresholds and reporting use odds ratios on the
   switched scale.  The `subgroup_notation = "benefit"` inversion
   applies identically.

4. **No CDE/AHR estimands**: these are survival-specific.  The binary
   DGM stores OR-scale effects in the `hazard_ratios` list for
   reporting compatibility.

5. **GRF standalone included**: the standalone GRF analysis
   (`grf.subg.harm.glm`) uses `causal_forest()` for candidate
   factor screening and policy trees for subgroup identification.

## Key Difference from the Prior Discretised Setup

The prior version of this document discretised every continuous
covariate into a binary factor (using the same cuts that define
the true subgroup $Q$) before the analysis step.  That setup
implicitly gives the analysis methods knowledge of the true
cutpoints.  **This document feeds raw continuous covariates
(`age`, `preanti`, `wtkg`, `karnof`, `cd40`, `cd80`) to the
analysis methods**, so the search methods must discover cuts
themselves.  The DGM construction is unchanged: the true $Q$ is
still $\{\text{age} > 34\} \cap \{\text{preanti} \leq 744.5\}$
and the calibration targets the same OR(Q).

**Expected consequences** relative to the discretised run:

- Lower sensitivity and PPV for both FS and GRF, because
  discovered cuts will generally differ from the true cuts.
- Similar or slightly higher FPR for GRF, because the policy-tree
  search space is larger over continuous inputs.
- Detection power depends on how closely the median / GRF-derived
  cuts align with the true cuts.

## Limitations

- The binary DGM is based on a logistic regression fitted to
  the observed ACTG175 data.  The super-population preserves
  the empirical covariate distribution but assumes the logistic
  model is correctly specified.

- `k_inter` is a direct additive shift on the log-odds scale
  for Q members under treatment.  Positive values increase the
  outcome for Q; negative values decrease it.

- `dmin.grf` was calibrated on the discretised setup; a fresh
  calibration run with raw continuous inputs is recommended
  before production scaling.

## Reloading Saved Results

When `save_results = TRUE`, the simulation bundle is saved as an
`.rds` file in the `_data/` directory.  The bundle carries every
scalar, list, and object the vignette reads downstream of the
simulation run, which makes it straightforward to (a) reload for
interactive analysis or (b) split this document into a separate
"run" script and a "report" document in the future.

```r
bundle <- readRDS(
  "../_data/actg175_binary_benefit_simulations_rawcont_100alts_100nulls.rds"
)

# -- Core results (data.tables) --------------------------------------------
results_alt  <- bundle$results_alt
results_null <- bundle$results_null

# -- DGM objects (class "glm_dgm") -----------------------------------------
dgm_calibrated <- bundle$dgm_calibrated
dgm_null       <- bundle$dgm_null

# -- Restore ALL vignette-scope scalars consumed downstream of the run -----
# (Assigning locally lets Section 8 chunks run unchanged against the
#  reloaded bundle.)
with(bundle$config, {
  sim_n_sample        <<- n_sample
  nsims_alt           <<- nsims_alt
  nsims_null          <<- nsims_null
  n_workers           <<- n_workers
  confounders_analysis<<- confounders_analysis
  sg_notation         <<- sg_notation
  sgdist_min_pct_alt  <<- sgdist_min_pct_alt
  sgdist_min_pct_null <<- sgdist_min_pct_null
  sgdist_top_k        <<- sgdist_top_k
  sgdist_show_other_alt  <<- sgdist_show_other_alt
  sgdist_show_other_null <<- sgdist_show_other_null
  grf_dmin            <<- grf_dmin
  prod_alt            <<- prod_alt
  prod_null           <<- prod_null
})

timings      <- bundle$timings
n_failed_alt <- bundle$n_failed_alt
n_failed_null<- bundle$n_failed_null

# -- True effects (convenience) --------------------------------------------
bundle$true_effects$or_Q     # OR(Q) on switched scale
bundle$true_effects$or_Qc    # OR(Qc)
bundle$true_effects$or_ITT   # OR(ITT)
bundle$true_effects$k_inter  # calibrated interaction shift

# -- FS / GRF parameter lists (passed to run_simulation_analysis) ----------
bundle$fs_params
bundle$grf_params

# -- Provenance ------------------------------------------------------------
bundle$timestamp         # when the run completed
bundle$R_version         # R version used
bundle$fs_version        # forestsearch version used

# -- Reproduce Section 8 tables with the reloaded objects ------------------
format_oc_results(results_alt,    subgroup_notation = sg_notation, ...)
build_estimation_table(results_alt, dgm = dgm_calibrated,
                        subgroup_notation = sg_notation, ...)
```


# Summary {#sec-summary}

```{r summary-compute}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Compute summary metrics"

mc_se <- function(p, n) sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n)
methods <- sort(unique(results_alt$analysis))

summ <- data.frame(Method = methods, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for (m in methods) {
  ra <- results_alt[results_alt$analysis == m, ]
  rn <- results_null[results_null$analysis == m, ]

  summ$alt_det[summ$Method == m]   <- mean(ra$any.H, na.rm = TRUE)
  summ$null_fpr[summ$Method == m]  <- mean(rn$any.H, na.rm = TRUE)
  summ$alt_sens[summ$Method == m]  <- mean(ra$sens, na.rm = TRUE)
  summ$alt_ppv[summ$Method == m]   <- mean(ra$ppv, na.rm = TRUE)
  summ$se_det[summ$Method == m]    <- mc_se(
    summ$alt_det[summ$Method == m], nrow(ra))
  summ$se_fpr[summ$Method == m]    <- mc_se(
    summ$null_fpr[summ$Method == m], nrow(rn))
}
```

## FS vs GRF Classification Concordance Across Simulations

Per-subject classification concordance between ForestSearch and GRF
is computed within each simulation replicate by
`run_simulation_analysis()` and stored as `agree.FS.GRF` and
`kappa.FS.GRF` columns.  When a method does not detect a subgroup,
it classifies all subjects to $Q^c$.

```{r sim-concordance}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Classification concordance (click to expand)"
#| results: asis

conc_col <- "agree.FS.GRF"
kappa_col <- "kappa.FS.GRF"

if (all(c(conc_col, kappa_col) %in% names(results_alt)) &&
    all(c("FS", "GRF") %in% methods)) {

  # One row per sim (take FS rows — concordance is per-sim, same on both)
  fs_alt  <- results_alt[results_alt$analysis == "FS", ]
  grf_alt <- results_alt[results_alt$analysis == "GRF", ]
  n       <- nrow(fs_alt)

  both     <- sum(fs_alt$any.H == 1 & grf_alt$any.H == 1)
  fs_only  <- sum(fs_alt$any.H == 1 & grf_alt$any.H == 0)
  grf_only <- sum(fs_alt$any.H == 0 & grf_alt$any.H == 1)
  neither  <- sum(fs_alt$any.H == 0 & grf_alt$any.H == 0)
  both_idx <- fs_alt$any.H == 1 & grf_alt$any.H == 1

  conc_df <- data.frame(
    Metric = c(
      "Mean agreement (%)",
      "SD agreement (%)",
      "Mean kappa",
      "SD kappa",
      "Median kappa",
      "Both detect",
      "FS only",
      "GRF only",
      "Neither",
      sprintf("Mean agreement | both detect (n = %d)", both),
      sprintf("Mean kappa | both detect (n = %d)",     both)
    ),
    Value = c(
      sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(fs_alt[[conc_col]],  na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%.1f", 100 * sd(fs_alt[[conc_col]],    na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%.3f",       mean(fs_alt[[kappa_col]], na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%.3f",       sd(fs_alt[[kappa_col]],   na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%.3f",       median(fs_alt[[kappa_col]], na.rm = TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", both,     100 * both     / n),
      sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", fs_only,  100 * fs_only  / n),
      sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", grf_only, 100 * grf_only / n),
      sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", neither,  100 * neither  / n),
      if (both > 0)
        sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(fs_alt[[conc_col]][both_idx],  na.rm = TRUE))
      else "\u2014",
      if (both > 0)
        sprintf("%.3f",         mean(fs_alt[[kappa_col]][both_idx], na.rm = TRUE))
      else "\u2014"
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  cat(gt::as_raw_html(
    gt::gt(conc_df,
           groupname_col = NULL) |>
      gt::tab_header(title = sprintf(
        "FS vs GRF classification concordance (%d sims)", n)) |>
      gt::tab_row_group(label = "Overall agreement",
                        rows = 1:5) |>
      gt::tab_row_group(label = "Detection patterns",
                        rows = 6:9) |>
      gt::tab_row_group(label = "Conditional on both detecting",
                        rows = 10:11) |>
      gt::row_group_order(groups = c(
        "Overall agreement",
        "Detection patterns",
        "Conditional on both detecting")) |>
      gt::cols_label(Metric = gt::md("**Metric**"),
                     Value  = gt::md("**Value**")) |>
      gt::tab_options(table.font.size = 11)
  ), "\n\n")

} else {
  cat("*Concordance columns not found in results.  Ensure",
      "`run_simulation_analysis()` was called with",
      "`run_fs = TRUE` and `run_grf = TRUE`.*\n\n")
}
```

```{r summary-findings}
time_df <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(sprintf("Per-replicate (H1), %d workers",  n_workers),
             sprintf("Per-replicate (H0), %d workers",  n_workers),
             "This run (total)",
             sprintf("Projected production (%d H1 + %d H0)",
                     prod_alt, prod_null)),
  Value  = c(sprintf("%.1f sec",  time_per_alt),
             sprintf("%.1f sec",  time_per_null),
             sprintf("%.1f min",  as.numeric(timings$total) / 60),
             sprintf("%.1f hours",
                     (prod_alt  * time_per_alt +
                      prod_null * time_per_null) / 3600)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

cat(gt::as_raw_html(
  gt::gt(time_df) |>
    gt::tab_header(title = "Timing") |>
    gt::cols_label(Metric = gt::md("**Metric**"),
                   Value  = gt::md("**Value**")) |>
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = 11)
), "\n\n")
```


# Appendix: Effect Measures and Outcome Direction Conventions {#sec-appendix-conventions}

*This appendix is a quick-lookup reference for this vignette's
directional configuration.  For comprehensive coverage across all
endpoint types -- including the eight-scenario decision table,
worked code examples for binary, continuous, count, and survival
outcomes, common pitfalls, and verification tests -- see the
standalone* [*ForestSearch Outcome Orientation Reference*](https://larry-leon.github.io/forestsearch/articles/forestsearch_outcome_orientation_guide.html) *vignette.*

## A.1 The unified harm-search convention

Every subgroup search in `forestsearch` uses a **single comparison
direction** throughout the pipeline.  In each candidate subgroup
$S$, the package checks whether the estimated treatment effect
satisfies

$$
\hat{\theta}(S) \;\geq\; c_1
$$

(`effect.threshold`), with the same direction reused for the
bootstrap consistency check, $\hat{\theta}(S_b) \geq c_2$.  This
comparison never flips.  The entire question of how to set up a
search reduces to: **how do I orient my data so the subgroup I
want to find produces $\hat{\theta}(S) > 0$ on the chosen effect
scale?**

Two transformations handle the orientations that don't satisfy
this naturally.  First, **benefit search** -- finding a subgroup
in which the original experimental treatment is *beneficial* --
is implemented by switching the treatment labels so the worse
arm becomes `treat = 1`.  A benefit subgroup of the original
experimental then appears as a harm subgroup of the
switched-treatment; magnitudes are inverted at reporting time
via `subgroup_notation = "benefit"`.  Second, when the user's
binary outcome is encoded on the positive scale (higher $Y$ =
better), the binary effect estimator can substitute $1 - Y$
before computing the OR -- this is what the `adverse_outcome`
flag controls in the FS estimator path.

The flag's *name* suggests an interpretive label ("the outcome
is adverse"), but mechanically what it does in the binary FS
estimator is **flip $Y$ to $1 - Y$ when `adverse_outcome = FALSE`,
and leave $Y$ as-is when `TRUE`** (the default for binary).  The
two framings -- pre-flip $Y$ at data prep and pass `TRUE`, or
keep $Y$ positive and pass `FALSE` -- are mechanically
equivalent for binary outcomes.  For **continuous** and **count**
outcomes the FS effect estimator does **not** auto-flip on the
flag (only the GRF candidate-cut step does); for those outcome
types you must encode $Y$ on the harm direction at data prep
and pass `adverse_outcome = TRUE`.  The simplest safe rule
across all GLM outcome types is therefore: **encode $Y$ on the
adverse scale at data prep and pass `adverse_outcome = TRUE`
everywhere**.  This is the convention used by the present
vignette; see @sec-stat-goals for the specific row that applies
and Section 1.1 for the data-prep step.

::: {.callout-tip title="DGM golden rule"}
Once the data is correctly oriented, build the DGM with **positive
`k_inter`**, a **positive calibration target**, and a **positive
`k_inter_range` grid**.  The DGM operates on the final, oriented
data; outcome and treatment manipulations (negation, switching)
happen at the data-prep step, *before* the DGM is constructed.
:::

## A.2 Effect scales and threshold conventions

`forestsearch` works on the **log scale** internally for ratio
measures and on the **identity scale** for additive measures.
This affects how `effect.threshold` is interpreted:

| Measure type | Examples | What `effect.threshold = c₁` becomes |
|--------------|----------|---------------------------------------|
| Ratio | HR, OR, IRR, RR | $\log(c_1)$ -- e.g., 1.25 → 0.223 |
| Additive (bounded) | RD, IRD | $c_1$ directly; bounded in $[-1, 1]$ |
| Additive (unbounded) | MD | $c_1$ directly; unbounded |

For RD and IRD, the package warns and remaps if the threshold
is set outside the bounded range.  For MD (mean difference) the
threshold is genuinely unbounded -- values like
30 cells/$\mu$L are legitimate, and the package no longer
remaps them as it once did when MD was incorrectly treated as a
bounded measure.  In all cases, the comparison the package
performs internally is $\hat{\theta} \geq$ (transformed
threshold), with $\hat{\theta}$ on the same scale (log for
ratios, identity for additives).


## A.3 Reference table

```{r appendix-conventions-table}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Build the master conventions table (click to expand)"

conv <- data.frame(
  Outcome   = c(rep("Binary",     4),
                rep("Continuous", 4),
                rep("Count",      4),
                rep("Survival",   2)),
  Measure   = c(rep("OR",  4),
                rep("MD",  4),
                rep("IRR", 4),
                rep("HR",  2)),
  Direction = c(
    "Positive (e.g., improvement = 1)",
    "Positive (e.g., improvement = 1)",
    "Adverse (e.g., death = 1)",
    "Adverse (e.g., death = 1)",
    "Positive (e.g., QoL score, higher = better)",
    "Positive (e.g., QoL score, higher = better)",
    "Adverse (e.g., pain score, higher = worse)",
    "Adverse (e.g., pain score, higher = worse)",
    "Positive (rare: e.g., recovery events)\u00b9",
    "Positive (rare: e.g., recovery events)\u00b9",
    "Adverse (e.g., adverse-event count)",
    "Adverse (e.g., adverse-event count)",
    "Event = adverse (fixed by causal_survival_forest)",
    "Event = adverse (fixed)"
  ),
  Goal      = rep(c("Harm", "Benefit"), 7),
  EncodeY   = c(
    "Y as-is", "Y as-is",         # binary positive
    "Y as-is", "Y as-is",         # binary adverse
    "Pre-flip: Y_use = -Y\u00b2",  # cont positive
    "Pre-flip: Y_use = -Y\u00b2",
    "Y as-is", "Y as-is",         # cont adverse
    "(see footnote 1)",            # count positive
    "(see footnote 1)",
    "Y as-is", "Y as-is",         # count adverse
    "Y as-is", "Y as-is"          # survival
  ),
  Treat     = rep(c("Original", "Switched"), 7),
  AdvFlag   = c(
    "FALSE", "FALSE",   # binary positive
    "TRUE",  "TRUE",    # binary adverse
    "TRUE",  "TRUE",    # cont positive (after pre-flip)
    "TRUE",  "TRUE",    # cont adverse
    "TRUE",  "TRUE",    # count positive
    "TRUE",  "TRUE",    # count adverse
    "(N/A)", "(N/A)"     # survival
  ),
  Notation  = rep(c("\"harm\"", "\"benefit\""), 7),
  Meaning   = c(
    # Binary
    "Trt reduces P(positive Y) in subgroup",
    "Orig-experimental increases P(positive Y) in subgroup",
    "Trt increases P(adverse Y) in subgroup",
    "Orig-experimental reduces P(adverse Y) in subgroup",
    # Continuous
    "Trt reduces Y (positive scale) in subgroup",
    "Orig-experimental increases Y (positive scale) in subgroup",
    "Trt increases Y (adverse scale) in subgroup",
    "Orig-experimental reduces Y (adverse scale) in subgroup",
    # Count
    "Trt reduces rate of (positive) events in subgroup",
    "Orig-experimental increases rate of (positive) events",
    "Trt increases rate of adverse events in subgroup",
    "Orig-experimental reduces rate of adverse events",
    # Survival
    "Trt increases hazard of event in subgroup",
    "Orig-experimental reduces hazard of event in subgroup"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Build gt
gt_conv <- gt::gt(conv, groupname_col = "Outcome", rowname_col = NULL) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    Measure   = gt::md("**Measure**"),
    Direction = gt::md("**Native Y direction**"),
    Goal      = gt::md("**Search goal**"),
    EncodeY   = gt::md("**Encode Y at data prep**"),
    Treat     = gt::md("**Treatment coding**"),
    AdvFlag   = gt::md("**`adverse_outcome`**"),
    Notation  = gt::md("**`subgroup_notation`**"),
    Meaning   = gt::md("**\"Effect > c\u2081\" means in subgroup**")
  ) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title    = "Effect measure / outcome-direction / search-goal combinations",
    subtitle = "User-facing settings for forestsearch() and grf.subg.harm.glm()"
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style    = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_row_groups()
  ) |>
  gt::tab_options(
    table.font.size = 10,
    row_group.padding = gt::px(4),
    data_row.padding  = gt::px(3)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_footnote(
    footnote = paste0(
      "Positive count outcomes are uncommon (count outcomes typically ",
      "model adverse events or rates).  If you have one, model the ",
      "complement (e.g., max-rate minus observed) on the adverse scale, ",
      "or consult the package authors."
    ),
    locations = gt::cells_body(
      columns = "Direction",
      rows    = which(conv$Outcome == "Count" & grepl("rare", conv$Direction))
    )
  ) |>
  gt::tab_footnote(
    footnote = paste0(
      "For continuous outcomes the FS effect estimator (`make_lm_estimator`) ",
      "does not respect `adverse_outcome`.  Pre-flip Y to the adverse direction ",
      "at data prep so OR / MD > threshold consistently indicates harm.  ",
      "GRF (`grf.subg.harm.glm`) does respect the flag for continuous; the ",
      "pre-flip + `adverse_outcome = TRUE` rule keeps both pipelines aligned."
    ),
    locations = gt::cells_body(
      columns = "EncodeY",
      rows    = which(conv$Outcome == "Continuous" &
                      grepl("Pre-flip", conv$EncodeY))
    )
  )

gt_conv
```

## A.4 Worked example: this vignette's configuration

The present vignette uses the row **Binary | OR | Adverse | Benefit**.
Concretely:

- The clinical concept is improvement (CD4 response by 20 weeks),
  but `y_binary` is encoded at data prep on the **adverse** scale
  as $I(\text{cd420} \leq \text{cd40})$ -- a 1 indicates failure
  to improve.
- Treatment is **switched** so ddI $\to$ `treat = 1` and
  ZDV+ddI $\to$ `treat = 0`.
- `adverse_outcome` defaults to `TRUE` for binary inside
  `forestsearch()` and is consistent with the adverse encoding
  of `y_binary`.
- The package's harm-search machinery flags subgroups where the
  switched treatment (ddI) increases the odds of non-improvement
  -- equivalently, where the original experimental (ZDV+ddI) is
  beneficial in giving improvement.
- Calibration target $\text{OR}(Q) = `r cal_target_or`$ corresponds
  to a $`r cal_target_or`\times$ odds-ratio of benefit for
  ZDV+ddI in $Q$.  This is the same magnitude as OR computed on
  the natural (original treatment, improvement-Y) scale, by the
  $\text{OR}(\text{switched, adverse}) = \text{OR}(\text{original, positive})$
  symmetry.
- Reporting uses `subgroup_notation = "benefit"` so summary tables
  display effect estimates on the original-experimental side.


## A.5 Common pitfalls

The standalone [*ForestSearch Outcome Orientation Reference*](https://larry-leon.github.io/forestsearch/articles/forestsearch_outcome_orientation_guide.html)
is the authoritative source for setup mechanics across all endpoint
types.  Two pitfalls show up often enough in practice to flag
here:

::: {.callout-warning title="Pitfall 1: calibration target on the wrong scale"}
Setting (e.g.) `cal_target_or = 0.5` together with a negative
`k_inter_range` produces a $Q$ that is only marginally more
extreme than the rest of the sample in the same direction --
no real contrast.  *Symptom:* near-100% detection paired with
very high false-positive rate (~97%).  *Fix:* use a target
above 1 with a positive `k_inter` grid for ratio measures, or
a positive target with a positive grid for MD.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Pitfall 2: `adverse_outcome` confused with outcome negation"}
Setting `adverse_outcome = FALSE` for a benefit search with
switched treatment and a *positive* binary outcome causes the
binary FS estimator to flip $Y \to 1 - Y$, reversing the OR
direction and breaking the $\hat{\theta} \geq c_1$ comparison.
*Symptom:* zero detection.  *Fix:* leave `adverse_outcome` at
its default `TRUE` for binary, *or* pre-flip $Y$ at data prep
(the convention used by this vignette -- see @sec-stat-goals).
:::

For the full list of pitfalls -- including MD-threshold remapping
behaviour, survival with positive events, and DGM construction
gotchas -- the eight-scenario decision table, the four
verification tests, and worked code examples for binary,
continuous, count, and survival outcomes, see the standalone
[*ForestSearch Outcome Orientation Reference*](https://larry-leon.github.io/forestsearch/articles/forestsearch_outcome_orientation_guide.html)
vignette.
